issues.title: shared/apm.md restores via apm-action's tar fallback because the apm CLI is never installed; skills land in unpredictable paths
issues.body:
## Summary

Every restore step driven by `shared/apm.md` runs `microsoft/apm-action` in its **tar-only fallback** mode (`APM not available — extracting with tar (no verification)…`), because nothing in the shared workflow or the action installs the `apm` CLI on the runner. The fallback uses `tar xzf <bundle> -C <workspace> --strip-components=1`, which is bundle-layout-naive and doesn't replicate the CLI's package-aware deployment. Whether the agent later finds skills depends on whether the bundle's directory layout happens to match what the agent's skill-loader expects — i.e., a coincidence we don't control.

## Repro

Any gh-aw workflow that imports `shared/apm.md`. Concrete example: https://github.com/elastic/docs-actions/blob/main/.github/workflows/gh-aw-docs-review.lock.yml

This is the relevant fragment in the agent job (gh-aw v0.71.1 — same shape in v0.71.4):

```yaml
- name: Restore APM packages
  uses: microsoft/apm-action@a190b0b1a91031057144dc136acf9757a59c9e4d # v1.4.1
  with:
    bundle: \${{ steps.apm_bundle.outputs.path }}
```

Note: no preceding step installs the `apm` CLI. The same is true in `microsoft/apm`'s own `shared/apm.md` head — it pins `microsoft/apm-action@v1.6.0` but doesn't add a setup-apm step.

## Observed behavior

In `elastic/docs-content`, the agent log for every APM-importing workflow contains:

```
Restoring bundle: /tmp/gh-aw/apm-workspace/build/inline-workflow-1.0.0.tar.gz
APM not available — extracting with tar (no verification)...
[command]/usr/bin/tar xzf /tmp/gh-aw/apm-workspace/build/inline-workflow-1.0.0.tar.gz \
  -C /home/runner/work/docs-content/docs-content --strip-components=1
Restored N file(s) (unverified — install APM for integrity checks)
```

Where `N` varies between 0, 10, and 36 across runs of similar shape. After the extract, `skill(<name>)` calls fail with `Skill not found`, and the agent falls back to manual analysis (e.g., \"All skills are unavailable. I'll review the changes using my own judgment now.\").

This same fallback ran on a working April 27 run that *did* find skills, and on May 5 runs that didn't. Same action version, same bundle source, same caller — only the bundle's internal layout differed (different skill version and additional skills packed in due to a separate cache-key issue we filed at github/gh-aw#30365).

## Suggested fix

One of:

1. **Install the `apm` CLI in the shared workflow before invoking `microsoft/apm-action`.** A setup-apm step in `apm-prep` (and a matching one before the agent job's restore call when the shared workflow inlines into gh-aw lock files) would put the action on the supported path and avoid the fallback entirely.
2. **Make the tar fallback fail loudly** rather than silently extracting with `--strip-components=1`. Today it logs a parenthetical note, exits 0, and leaves the consumer thinking the bundle was deployed. A loud failure would surface the missing CLI immediately.
3. **At minimum, document `shared/apm.md` as requiring the CLI** and make the install path obvious.

Happy to test a fix in a docs-actions workflow if helpful.

## Versions

- Caller: `elastic/docs-content`
- Library: `elastic/docs-actions` (gh-aw v0.71.1, also reproduced under v0.71.4)
- `microsoft/apm-action`: `v1.4.1` (current gh-aw v0.71.1 pin) and `v1.6.0` (current `shared/apm.md` head)

## Related

- github/gh-aw#30365 — APM cache key collides across reusable workflows. Pairs with this: even after we made bundles consistent across our workflows, the tar fallback still drops files in the wrong layout.

issues.title: Docs: clarify install-time discovery rules for marketplace-published plugins (`.apm/<type>/` vs root convention dirs)
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Authoring a multi-plugin marketplace publisher repo today requires reading APM's integrator source code to figure out the right source layout. The pack-distribute and marketplace-authoring guides imply a layout that silently breaks at install time for half the primitive types.

**Concrete ask (docs-only):** add a per-primitive scan-path table sourced from the integrators, recommend `.apm/<type>/` as the symmetric canonical layout for marketplace publishers, and add a worked example of a multi-plugin publisher repo (top-level `marketplace:` + per-plugin `apm.yml` + per-plugin `apm pack`).

## Problem

The "convention dirs" layout shown for `apm pack` in the [pack-distribute guide](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/pack-distribute/) (i.e. `agents/`, `skills/`, `commands/`, `instructions/`, `hooks/` at plugin root) is **asymmetric between the pack-export code path and the install-integrate code path**.

- `apm pack` (liberal): accepts both `.apm/<type>/` AND root `<type>/` for all primitive types.
- `apm install` (per-integrator, stricter): only `agents` and `skills` accept root `<type>/`. **Instructions, commands, hooks, and mcps are scanned ONLY under `.apm/<type>/`.**

As a marketplace publisher, this means if I author a plugin with `instructions/foo.instructions.md` at plugin root (per the docs), `apm pack` happily includes my file in the bundle — but downstream `apm install` silently drops it. No warning, no error, no doc that flags this.

This bit me hard while building [`DevExpGbb/zava-agent-config`](https://github.com/DevExpGbb/zava-agent-config) (a multi-plugin marketplace publisher used for an enterprise demo). Debugging took ~half a day; the only way to discover the gap was reading `instruction_integrator.py`.

## What I expected from the docs

That the "convention dirs" pattern shown as the canonical `apm pack` output (per [Bundle structure → Single plugin per repo](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/pack-distribute/#single-plugin-per-repo) and the [remap table](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/pack-distribute/#bundle-structure-plugin-format-default)) would also be the layout that consumers see and that integrators scan at install time. The remap table even shows `.apm/instructions/*.instructions.md` → `instructions/*.instructions.md` as the deployed shape — implying parity. Nothing on [pack-distribute](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/pack-distribute/), [marketplace-authoring](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/marketplace-authoring/), or [marketplaces](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/marketplaces/) mentions that authoring directly into root `instructions/` (without `.apm/`) will be silently dropped at install time.

## What actually happens

Two scan modes diverge:

**Pack-export** (liberal — accepts both layouts):

- `_collect_apm_components()` scans `.apm/{agents,skills,prompts,instructions,commands}` — `src/apm_cli/bundle/plugin_exporter.py:~83`
- `_collect_root_plugin_components()` scans root `{agents,skills,commands,instructions}` — `src/apm_cli/bundle/plugin_exporter.py:~111`

**Install-integrate** (per-integrator, stricter):

| Integrator | Source | Scans `.apm/<type>/` | Scans root `<type>/` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AgentIntegrator.find_agent_files` | [`integration/agent_integrator.py:40-64`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/agent_integrator.py#L40-L64) | ✅ `.apm/agents/`, `.apm/chatmodes/` | ✅ `<root>/*.agent.md`, `<root>/*.chatmode.md` |
| `SkillIntegrator._integrate_skill_bundle` | [`integration/skill_integrator.py:1029+`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/skill_integrator.py#L1029) | ✅ `.apm/skills/` | ✅ `<root>/skills/<name>/` (only when `package_type ∈ {MARKETPLACE_PLUGIN, SKILL_BUNDLE}`) |
| `InstructionIntegrator.find_instruction_files` | [`integration/instruction_integrator.py:35-44`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/instruction_integrator.py#L35-L44) | ✅ | ❌ **hard-coded `subdirs=[".apm/instructions"]`** |
| `CommandIntegrator.find_prompt_files` | [`integration/command_integrator.py:185`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/command_integrator.py#L185) | ✅ `.apm/prompts/` | ❌ |
| `HookIntegrator` | [`integration/hook_integrator.py:282`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py#L282) | ✅ `.apm/hooks/` | ❌ |

Net: agents and skills tolerate root convention-dirs at install time; instructions, commands, hooks, mcps do not.

## Concrete failure I hit

In `zava-agent-config v2.0.0`, plugins followed the convention-dirs pattern shown in the pack docs:

- `plugins/<kit>/agents/security.agent.md` → ✅ deploys (root `*.agent.md` glob)
- `plugins/<kit>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` → ✅ deploys (`MARKETPLACE_PLUGIN` branch in `SkillIntegrator`)
- `plugins/<kit>/instructions/<x>.instructions.md` → ❌ **silently does not deploy** — only `.apm/instructions/` is scanned

`apm pack` showed the file in the bundle, so authoring-side feedback was green. The gap surfaced only when a downstream consumer ran `apm install` and noticed agent prompts weren't picking up the rules. No warning, no doc page, no per-primitive layout reference.

## How I resolved it (validates the recommended layout)

[`zava-agent-config v4.0.0`](https://github.com/DevExpGbb/zava-agent-config/releases/tag/v4.0.0) standardizes on `plugins/<kit>/.apm/<type>/` for **every** primitive type. Verified end-to-end:

1. **Install side (`apm install`):** all 7 primitives across 4 plugins deploy correctly — 2 agents, 2 skills, 3 instructions. [Storefront PR (merged)](https://github.com/DevExpGbb/zava-storefront/pull/1) shows green CI on `apm audit --ci`.

2. **Pack side (`apm pack` per-kit):** with a per-plugin `apm.yml` (containing minimal `dependencies: apm: []` to satisfy the "neither dependencies nor marketplace" check), `apm pack --offline` correctly:
   - synthesizes `plugin.json` from `apm.yml` metadata into `build/<name>-<version>/plugin.json`
   - remaps `.apm/agents/*.agent.md` → `agents/*.agent.md`
   - remaps `.apm/skills/<name>/` → `skills/<name>/`
   - emits a clean Anthropic-shape plugin bundle ready to publish

So the symmetric `.apm/<type>/` source layout is the canonical layout that satisfies both code paths simultaneously. The docs just don't say so.

## What would help

A docs section (probably an addition to [pack-distribute](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/pack-distribute/) or a new "Plugin layout reference" page) that:

1. **Documents the asymmetry explicitly** — pack-export is liberal, install-integrate is stricter and per-primitive.
2. **Provides a per-primitive scan-path table** like the one above, sourced from the integrators rather than the pack exporter, so authors know what consumers will actually see at install time.
3. **Recommends `.apm/<type>/` as the symmetric canonical layout** for ALL primitives in a multi-plugin marketplace publisher repo — i.e. tell authors "use `.apm/<type>/` and both code paths agree; use root convention dirs and only agents+skills will work."
4. **Shows a worked example of a marketplace publisher repo with multiple plugins**, each as a self-contained APM package: per-plugin `apm.yml` + `.apm/<type>/` source tree + per-plugin `apm pack` to emit `plugin.json`, plus a top-level `apm pack` to emit `marketplace.json`. The current [marketplace-authoring](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/marketplace-authoring/) guide covers the marketplace block beautifully but stops short of showing the in-plugin source layout, and the pack-distribute "Multi-plugin repo" section is similarly silent on per-plugin source layout. [`zava-agent-config`](https://github.com/DevExpGbb/zava-agent-config) at v4.0.0 is a working reference if useful as a starting point.

## Scope

This is a **docs-only ask** — please do not treat it as a request to change integrator behavior. Whether the install-time scanners _should_ also accept root convention dirs (matching the pack exporter) is a separate behavior question I'm happy to file as a follow-up if useful. For now I just want the docs to reflect what the code actually does, so the next author building a marketplace publisher repo doesn't lose half a day to silent-drop debugging.

## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-05-07

#### `apm deps update --target` omits `windsurf` from accepted values
- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: The `--target` help text does not list `windsurf` as a valid value, even though `windsurf` is fully supported by the underlying `TargetParamType`. The `apm install --target` help correctly includes `windsurf`. This inconsistency will cause users to miss that `windsurf` is a valid target for `apm deps update`.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm deps update --help` shows: `Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, agent-skills, all.`
  - `apm install --help` shows: `Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, windsurf, agent-skills, all.`
  - Source confirms `windsurf` IS valid: `src/apm_cli/commands/deps/cli.py` line 700-704 uses `TargetParamType()` but has a hand-written help string that omits windsurf.
  - The docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli-commands.md` line 1097) also list `windsurf` as valid for `apm deps update`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--target` help string in `src/apm_cli/commands/deps/cli.py` to add `windsurf` after `gemini`: `"Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, windsurf, agent-skills, all."`

---

#### `apm cache clean` has two redundant flags doing the same thing
- **Command**: `apm cache clean`
- **Problem**: Both `-f, --force` and `-y, --yes` are documented as "Skip confirmation prompt". Having two flags with different names for the exact same behavior is confusing and inconsistent with the rest of the CLI, which uses `-y/--yes` as the convention for skip-confirmation (e.g., `apm deps clean`, `apm marketplace remove`, `apm runtime remove`).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm cache clean --help
  Options:
    -f, --force  Skip confirmation prompt
    -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt
  ```
  Source (`src/apm_cli/commands/cache.py` lines 58-74): both flags are checked with `if not force and not yes:`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove `-f/--force` from `apm cache clean` to unify on `-y/--yes` for confirmation-skipping, matching the pattern used by all other commands. Alternatively, keep `--force` as a hidden alias if backward compatibility is required.

---

#### `apm mcp install` options appear as disconnected epilog text rather than proper CLI options
- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: `apm mcp install` uses `ignore_unknown_options` and `allow_extra_args` to forward arguments to `apm install --mcp`. Its supported flags (`--transport`, `--url`, `--env`, `--header`, `--registry`, `--mcp-version`, `--dev`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--verbose`, `--no-policy`) are shown as free-form epilog text, not as registered Click options. Users cannot discover individual flag descriptions via `--help`.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp install --help
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --mcp --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL    Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE    Environment variable (repeatable)...
  ```
  The epilog is rendered as a block of unformatted text after the Options section.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) register the key options explicitly on `mcp install` so they appear properly in `--help`, or (b) rewrite the epilog to be clearly formatted with line breaks and indentation so the hint text is readable. Option (b) is lower effort and preserves the passthrough design. Example: split each option onto its own line in the epilog string.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm deps tree` docs omit the `--global` flag
- **Command**: `apm deps tree`
- **Problem**: The CLI reference docs at `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli-commands.md` (around line 1000-1026) document `apm deps tree` with no Options section. The actual CLI has a `-g, --global` flag.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps tree --help
  Options:
    -g, --global  Show user-scope dependency tree (~/.apm/)
    --help        Show this message and exit.
  ```
  The docs only show a code block `apm deps tree` with no options listed.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add an Options section to the `apm deps tree` documentation listing `-g, --global`.

---

#### `apm update` documentation example output uses emoji, violating the ASCII-only encoding rule
- **Command**: `apm update`
- **Problem**: The docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli-commands.md` around line 829) show a sample update notification that includes the emoji `warning sign + variation selector`. The project encoding rules mandate all CLI output and docs stay within printable ASCII (U+0020-U+007E). The correct convention per the codebase is `[!]`.
- **Evidence**: The sample output block in the docs reads:
  ```
  [warning emoji]  A new version of APM is available: 0.7.0 (current: 0.6.3)
  Run apm update to upgrade
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Replace the warning emoji with `[!]` in the example output block:
  ```
  [!] A new version of APM is available: 0.7.0 (current: 0.6.3)
  Run apm update to upgrade
  ```

---

#### `apm compile` auto-detection table uses deprecated target alias `vscode`
- **Command**: `apm compile`
- **Problem**: The auto-detection table in the docs lists `vscode` as a detected target name (condition: "`.github/` exists only"). However `vscode` is a deprecated alias for `copilot`. Users reading the table may expect to see `vscode` as output from `apm targets` but the CLI now uses `copilot` as the canonical name.

- **Suggested Fix**: Update the auto-detection table to use `copilot` instead of `vscode` in the Target column.

The following commands and areas passed all checks with no issues found:

issues.title: extends: org also fails to layer dependencies.require from parent (same root as #1198)
issues.body:
## Summary

Same root cause as #1198 (`unmanaged_files` not layered through `extends: org`). The `dependencies.require` field is also dropped when a repo `apm-policy.yml` declares `extends: org` and the org floor declares `dependencies.require`.

## Repro

```yaml
# Org floor (e.g. org/.github/apm-policy.yml)
version: 1
dependencies:
  require:
    - secure-baseline
```

```yaml
# Repo override (e.g. some-app/apm-policy.yml)
version: 1
extends: org
# (does NOT redeclare dependencies.require)
```

Run `apm audit --ci --policy ./apm-policy.yml` in the repo with `secure-baseline` removed from `apm.yml`. Expected: `required-packages` check fails with `secure-baseline missing from manifest`. Actual: check passes with `No required packages configured` — the org's required list never made it into the layered policy.

## Workaround (proven)

Redeclare in the repo override:

```yaml
version: 1
extends: org
dependencies:
  require:
    - secure-baseline   # workaround: extends: org doesn't layer this
```

## Why this matters

Defeats the **"required floor"** governance pattern that the policy reference (https://microsoft.github.io/apm/enterprise/policy-reference/) is documented to support. Org wants to mandate `secure-baseline` everywhere; `extends: org` is the documented mechanism; today it silently downgrades the floor.

## Likely fix location

Same place as #1198 — the inheritance-merge code path that handles `extends:`. Looks like an additive/union merge is missing for `dependencies.require` (and possibly `dependencies.deny`, untested).

## Context

Discovered while wiring a 5-beat enterprise demo. Repro is reproducible end-to-end on a public org. Same workaround as #1198 unblocks; would prefer a fix so policy authors don't have to remember to redeclare two separate fields per override file.

issues.title: feat: make `apm update` respect air-gapped environment variables
issues.body:
## Context

Follow-up to #660, which made `install.sh` configurable for air-gapped / GHE environments via `GITHUB_URL`, `REPO`, and `VERSION` env vars.

## Problem

The `apm update` command (and the underlying version-checker) does not honour those same environment variables:

1. **Version check** -- the latest-version lookup always targets the public GitHub API, ignoring `GITHUB_URL` and `REPO`. In an air-gapped network this call will time out or fail.
2. **Installer download** -- the update command fetches the install script from a hardcoded public URL. Even though the downloaded `install.sh` itself now supports the env vars, the download step has no way to reach the script when the public internet is unavailable.

## Expected behaviour

`apm update` should respect the same `GITHUB_URL`, `REPO`, and `VERSION` env vars that `install.sh` supports, so that:

- The version check queries the correct API host.
- The installer script is fetched from the correct mirror / internal host.
- Setting `VERSION` skips the API call entirely (matching `install.sh` behaviour).

## Additional notes

- The `--check` flag should also work against the configured host.
- The version-checker utility used by the update-available notification on every CLI invocation has the same issue and should be fixed together.

issues.title: fix(deps): bare cache incompatible with git 2.53.0 safe.bareRepository + fetched SHAs not ref-reachable
issues.body:
## Summary

Two bugs in `bare_cache.py` discovered during E2E validation of the SHA-pin fix (#1258 / PR #1259):

### Bug 1: `git -C <bare>` fails on git 2.53.0

Git 2.53.0 (Homebrew, macOS) defaults `safe.bareRepository=explicit`. All bare-repo git commands in `bare_cache.py` use `git -C <path>` which now fails with exit 128 on bare repos. The fix is to use `git --git-dir <path>` instead (8 locations).

### Bug 2: Fetched SHAs are not ref-reachable for `git clone --local --shared`

When `fetch_sha_into_bare` fetches a specific SHA into an existing bare, the SHA lands in the object store but is not pointed to by any ref. `git clone --local --shared` from a shallow bare uses upload-pack (ignoring `--local`) and only transfers objects reachable from advertised refs -- so the orphaned SHA is silently omitted and `git checkout <sha>` fails in the consumer.

The fix creates a synthetic `refs/heads/apm-pin-<sha12>` ref after every successful fetch (or discovery) so the SHA is reachable via the default refspec.

## Reproduction

Both bugs are exercised by installing a mono-repo package with SHA-pinned transitive deps on git 2.53.0. The E2E test repo `sergio-sisternes-epam/apm-marketplace-tests` reproduces this scenario.

## Environment

- macOS (Darwin)
- Git 2.53.0 with `safe.bareRepository=explicit` (default)
- APM built from main (post PR #1259 merge)

  ```
  Meanwhile, `apm config --help` lists only `get`, `set`, `unset` — no hint of `list`, no hint that bare `get` lists everything.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) add a `list` alias/subcommand that calls `apm config get` with no argument (consistent with the rest of the CLI), or (b) rename `get` with no argument to make the listing behavior more prominent in help text. Option (a) is preferred for consistency with `apm deps list`, `apm mcp list`, `apm runtime list`.

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm mcp install --help` renders forwarded options as unstructured epilog text

- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: The help output for `apm mcp install` lists only `--help` as a formal Click option. All other relevant flags (`--transport`, `--url`, `--env`, `--header`, `--registry`, `--mcp-version`, `--dev`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--verbose`, `--no-policy`) appear as an unformatted text block after the Options section. This makes them undiscoverable through standard `--help` use and breaks the structural pattern of every other command in the CLI.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --mcp --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
  In contrast, `apm mcp search --help`, `apm mcp show --help`, and all other commands expose properly typed options with defaults.
- **Suggested Fix**: Surface these forwarded options as real Click options (or at minimum delegate the full `--help` to `apm install --mcp --help` automatically). The epilog blob provides no type information, no defaults, and no descriptions.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm config --help` does not hint at bare `apm config` table behavior

- **Command**: `apm config`
- **Problem**: Running `apm config` with no subcommand shows a rich configuration table (project name, version, MCP count, global CLI version, etc.). This is useful and documented in `docs/reference/cli/config.md`, but `apm config --help` gives no indication this behavior exists. Users who read only the help text will not discover it.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config --help
  Usage: apm config [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

    Configure APM CLI

  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

  Commands:
    get    Get a configuration value
    set    Set a configuration value
    unset  Unset a configuration value
  ```
  No mention that bare `apm config` shows a summary table.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a one-line note in the command description or epilog, e.g. "Run with no subcommand to print a merged project + global configuration table."

#### `apm deps update` has no deprecation notice despite overlap with `apm update`

- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: `apm install --help` explicitly warns that its `--update` flag is deprecated in favor of `apm update`, calling it "deprecated: prefer 'apm update' for an interactive plan". However, `apm deps update` — which also updates dependencies — carries no such deprecation or cross-reference notice. This leaves users uncertain about whether `apm deps update` and `apm update` are equivalent, and which one is preferred.
- **Evidence**:
  From `apm install --help`:
  ```
  --update   Update dependencies to latest Git references
             (deprecated: prefer 'apm update' for an interactive plan,
             or 'apm update --yes' for CI)
  ```
  From `apm deps update --help`:
  ```
  Usage: apm deps update [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...

    Update APM dependencies to latest refs
  ```
  No deprecation notice, no reference to `apm update`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a note to `apm deps update` help text indicating its relationship to `apm update` (e.g. "`apm update` is the recommended alternative for interactive update workflows"). If `apm deps update` is fully supported and distinct (it accepts `[PACKAGES...]` for selective update), clarify this distinction in the description.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks:

- `apm --help` — complete, well-structured
- `apm init --help` — clear options, consistent style
- `apm install --help` — comprehensive, accurate flag descriptions and defaults
- `apm uninstall --help` — consistent flags (`--dry-run`, `-v`, `-g`)
- `apm update --help` — clear, flags match docs
- `apm compile --help` — thorough, all flags match docs
- `apm run --help` — concise and correct
- `apm deps list/tree/info/clean --help` — all accurate and well-described
- `apm mcp list/search/show --help` — correctly formatted, defaults accurate (`list`: 20, `search`: 10)
- `apm config get/set --help` — accurate
- `apm runtime setup/list/status/remove --help` — all present, flags match docs (`-y/--yes` on `remove` confirmed)
- Error handling — `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (no arg), `apm config set` (no arg) all return clean usage errors, no stack traces
- Documentation cross-reference — all commands with CLI reference pages (`docs/reference/cli/*.md`) exist in the CLI; no documented commands are missing from the implementation

issues.title: [BUG] Cross-repo plugins on *.ghe.com marketplaces silently route auth at github.com
issues.body:
## Context

Discovered during review of PR #1292 (which fixed the in-marketplace variant of this class for #1285). When a `*.ghe.com` marketplace references a cross-repo plugin via dict source with a bare `repo` field, the resolver emits a bare canonical and downstream `DependencyReference.parse` defaults to `github.com` -- the same silent auth mis-route #1285 fixed for in-marketplace sources.

## Reproduce

Marketplace registered on `corp.ghe.com`. `marketplace.json` plugin entry:

```json
{
  "name": "shared-tool",
  "source": {
    "type": "github",
    "repo": "platform-team/shared-tool",
    "path": "plugins/shared"
  }
}
```

Then:

```
apm install shared-tool@my-marketplace --verbose
```

Verbose trace shows `Auth resolved: host=github.com` even though the marketplace is registered on `corp.ghe.com`. If `platform-team/shared-tool` lives on `corp.ghe.com` the install 401s with no actionable hint pointing at the misconfiguration; if it lives on `github.com` the install silently works.

## Why this is not part of PR #1292

The cross-repo case cannot be safely treated the same way at resolver-time. Two legitimate intents share the same surface syntax:

- **Intentional cross-host case**: marketplace on `corp.ghe.com`, plugin entry `repo: opensource-org/awesome-tool` (bare) meaning "github.com open-source dep". Today this works correctly (parse falls back to `github.com`, which is what the author meant).
- **Misconfigured case**: marketplace on `corp.ghe.com`, plugin entry `repo: platform-team/shared-tool` (bare) meaning "the same enterprise host". Today this silently 401s.

A resolver-time always-on warning would false-positive on the intentional case and train operators to ignore the signal. PR #1292 explicitly scoped the host-prefix backfill to `_is_in_marketplace_source` to avoid changing semantics for cross-repo entries.

## Suggested approach

Surface the diagnostic at install-time when auth actually fails. When `apm install <plugin>@<marketplace>` returns 401 against `github.com` and the marketplace's host is `*.ghe.com`, emit an actionable hint such as:

> Auth failed against `github.com` for plugin `shared-tool@my-marketplace`. The marketplace is registered on `corp.ghe.com` -- did you mean to host-qualify the plugin's `repo` field as `corp.ghe.com/platform-team/shared-tool` in `marketplace.json`?

This belongs in the install error-handler (where the 401 surfaces with full host/auth context), not the resolver.

## Related

- PR: #1292
- Origin issue: #1285
- Test that locks current (pre-existing) behaviour: `test_cross_repo_source_not_prefixed` in `tests/unit/marketplace/test_marketplace_resolver.py`

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-05-14
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-05-14
**APM Version**: 0.13.0 (22ebb35)
**Commands Inspected**: 24 (`apm` + 6 core + 5 `deps` subcommands + 4 `mcp` subcommands + 3 `config` subcommands + 2 `runtime` subcommands + `apm mcp list`)

---

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 0     |
| Medium   | 3     |
| Low      | 1     |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm mcp install --help` produces unreadable, unstructured option text

- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: The "Common options" block is appended as a single unformatted text paragraph below the `--help` option, not as properly structured CLI option flags. This is inconsistent with every other command in the CLI and makes the help text very hard to read.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --mcp --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
  Compare with `apm mcp search --help` or any other command which formats options cleanly.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either expose the forwarded flags as actual Click options on the `mcp install` command, or restructure the help epilog into a readable table/list format with proper line breaks. The current paragraph blob is not actionable for users.

---

#### `apm deps list` -- two flags missing from reference documentation

- **Command**: `apm deps list --help`
- **Problem**: The flags `--all` and `--insecure` exist in the CLI but are not documented in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`.
- **Evidence** (CLI output):
  ```
  Options:
    -g, --global  List user-scope dependencies (~/.apm/) instead of project
    --all         Show both project and user-scope dependencies
    --insecure    Show only installed dependencies locked to (redacted) sources
    --help        Show this message and exit.
  ```
  The docs table for `apm deps list` only documents `-g, --global`:
  > | `-g, --global` | List user-scope dependencies in `~/.apm/` instead of the project. |
- **Suggested Fix**: Add rows for `--all` and `--insecure` to the `apm deps list` option table in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`.

---

#### `apm deps update` -- three flags missing from reference documentation

- **Command**: `apm deps update --help`
- **Problem**: The flags `--parallel-downloads`, `-g/--global`, and `--legacy-skill-paths` exist in the CLI but are not documented in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`.
- **Evidence** (CLI output):
  ```
  Options:
    -v, --verbose                 Show detailed update information
    --force                       Overwrite locally-authored files on collision
    -t, --target TARGET           Target platform (comma-separated). ...
    --parallel-downloads INTEGER  Max concurrent package downloads (0 to disable
                                  parallelism)  [default: 4]
    -g, --global                  Update user-scope dependencies (~/.apm/)
    --legacy-skill-paths          Deploy skill files to per-client paths ...
    --help                        Show this message and exit.
  ```
  The docs table for `apm deps update` only documents `-v/--verbose`, `--force`, and `-t/--target`:
  > There is no `--no-policy` flag; the only escape hatch is `APM_POLICY_DISABLE=1`
- **Suggested Fix**: Add rows for `--parallel-downloads`, `-g/--global`, and `--legacy-skill-paths` to the `apm deps update` option table in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm config` bare invocation undocumented in `--help` output

- **Command**: `apm config`
- **Problem**: Running `apm config` with no subcommand displays a useful merged project + global configuration table. However, `apm config --help` only lists subcommands (`get`, `set`, `unset`) and gives no hint that the bare invocation has useful behavior. New users may not discover this.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm config --help shows:
  Commands:
    get    Get a configuration value
    set    Set a configuration value
    unset  Unset a configuration value

  # But apm config (bare) shows a rich table:
                   Current APM Configuration
  ┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
  ┃ Category     ┃ Setting          ┃ Value                      ┃
  ...
  ```
  (The behavior is documented in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/config.md` but not surfaced in the terminal help.)
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a one-line note to the `apm config` group help string, e.g. `"Configure APM CLI. Run without a subcommand to show current configuration."` so users discover this from the terminal.

---

### Clean Areas

- **All 25 top-level commands** are present in both `apm --help` and `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`. No orphan commands on either side.
- **Error handling**: All tested error paths (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with no args, `apm config set` with no args) return clean usage errors -- no stack traces.
- **`apm config list`**: Not a CLI bug -- the subcommand is correctly `get`/`set`/`unset`, consistent with docs.
- **`apm mcp list`**: Fully functional; default limit of 20 matches docs.
- **`apm mcp search`**: Default limit 10 (different from list's 20) is intentional and documented correctly.
- **Flag consistency**: `--dry-run`, `-v/--verbose`, `-g/--global`, `-y/--yes` are consistently named across all commands that use them.
- **`--help` / `-h`**: Works correctly on every command and subcommand tested.
- **`apm deps update` `-t/--target`**: Present in CLI, documented in docs. Match confirmed.

issues.title: Producer experience: close the gap from "I built a plugin" to "every assistant can install it"
issues.body:
# Producer experience: close the gap from "I built a plugin" to "every assistant can install it"

## TL;DR

After #1281 (multi-profile marketplace outputs) and #1317 (filter-driven CLI + map-based manifest + `--json`), HEAD has the **runtime primitives** to publish any APM project to multiple AI assistants. What's missing is the **producer journey** that turns those primitives into a press-the-button release: discoverable repo shapes, a vendor-agnostic post-pack hint, scaffold templates that match real-world layouts, per-package versioning visibility, drift detection, and a `microsoft/apm-action` umbrella that absorbs the CI orchestration so producers don't hand-roll it.

This issue closes two community discussions ([#1322](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/discussions/1322) — jKlaus, monorepo plugin marketplace structure; [#1332](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/discussions/1332) — R. Collet, GitHub Releases for monorepo with per-package versions) by describing the full producer workflow APM should support, what works in HEAD today, and what we'll add to close the gap.

## Why now

Two real producers tried to ship multi-plugin marketplaces against `apm` 0.13 + the v0.14 surface and both stalled at the same step: they couldn't tell which repo shape APM expects, what `apm pack` should produce in a monorepo, whether to tag once or per-plugin, or how to wire a release workflow that publishes Claude **and** Codex artifacts in one go. None of these are missing engineering — they are missing surface, scaffolds, and CI primitives.

The win-condition this issue chases:

> A producer with a working plugin (or a folder of plugins) runs `apm init --shape=…`, gets a complete project skeleton including a release workflow that uses `microsoft/apm-action`, and is shipping multi-format marketplace artifacts on the next git tag — without writing a single shell script and without naming any one assistant's CLI in the output.

## Vendor-agnostic constraints (read first)

This issue is bounded by three non-negotiables drawn from APM's positioning:

1. **APM is vendor-agnostic.** Producer-facing output **must not** name a single consumer CLI (`copilot plugin install …`, `claude plugin marketplace add …`, `codex plugins install …`). Consumers may be on Copilot CLI, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Windsurf, or anything that ships next month. The post-pack experience must point producers at a docs page that lists all consumer paths, not a single one.
2. **`apm pack` is a release-time tool.** The dominant invocation site is CI/CD on a tag push — not local dev. Friction here multiplies: a missing `--json` parse or a forgotten `--marketplace` flag becomes a broken release.
3. **`microsoft/apm-action` is ours to evolve.** ([repo](https://github.com/microsoft/apm-action) — v1.6.0 floats `v1`.) Anything that's pure CI orchestration (matrix, drift PR, release notes, sha256 sidecars, GH Step Summary) belongs in the action, not as new CLI flags. Anything that's a portable validator (lockstep version check, dirty-tree check) belongs in the CLI as a thin additive flag so it works in GitLab/ADO/local pre-commit too.

Every recommendation below was checked against these three constraints before being proposed.

## What ships in HEAD today (verified against `apm 0.13.0` + Copilot CLI `1.0.48-1`)

| Capability | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `marketplace.outputs:` accepts map form `{claude: {}, codex: {path: …}}` | ✅ Shipped (#1317) | `src/apm_cli/marketplace/yml_schema.py:502-559` |
| List form `outputs: [claude, codex]` parses with deprecation warning | ✅ Shipped (#1317) | `yml_schema.py:586-595` |
| `apm pack --marketplace=<list\|all\|none>` filter | ✅ Shipped (#1317) | `src/apm_cli/commands/pack.py:129-138` |
| `apm pack --marketplace-path FORMAT=PATH` (repeatable) | ✅ Shipped (#1317) | `pack.py:140-148` |
| `apm pack --json` machine-readable to stdout | ✅ Shipped (#1317) | `pack.py:150-152` |
| `apm pack --offline` / `--include-prerelease` | ✅ Shipped | `pack.py` |
| `--marketplace-output` deprecated, auto-translates to `--marketplace-path claude=PATH` | ✅ Shipped (#1317), removal tracked in #1318 | `pack.py:195-207` |
| Per-package `tag_pattern: "{name}-v{version}"` for independent versions | ✅ Shipped, undocumented | `yml_schema.py:91-109`, `tag_pattern.py:52-103` |
| `apm init --plugin` and `apm marketplace init` exist as separate commands | ✅ Shipped | `commands/init.py:46-65`, `commands/marketplace/init.py:18-32` |
| Output formats supported by APM | **Two only**: `claude`, `codex` | `marketplace/output_profiles.py:67-91` |
| `apm pack` post-pack hint mentions Copilot/Claude/Codex CLIs | ❌ Vendor-neutral today (good) | `pack.py:373-406` |
| `apm marketplace doctor` checks format coverage / version alignment | ❌ Neither | `commands/marketplace/doctor.py` |
| `apm-action` passes `--marketplace`, `--marketplace-path`, `--json`, `--offline` to `apm pack` | ❌ Hardcoded only `-o`, `--format`, `--target`, `--archive` | `apm-action/src/bundler.ts:182-192` |

The CLI primitives are **already there**. The producer journey on top of them is not.

## The four repo shapes APM must serve

Today producers improvise. We should name the shapes, scaffold each one, and the rest of the issue then references them by name.

| Shape | When to use | apm.yml signature | What `apm pack` produces |
|---|---|---|---|
| **single-plugin** | One plugin, one repo (most plugins on GitHub today) | `plugin: {…}` + optional `marketplace:` | `build/<plugin>/` (bundle) + optional marketplace.json with one entry |
| **marketplace-aggregator** | Curate third-party plugins; no source in this repo | `marketplace:` only, all `source:` are remote `owner/repo[:path]` | `build/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` + per-format siblings |
| **marketplace-monorepo** | Many first-party plugins shipped together (Zava, jKlaus, Collet) | `marketplace:` + every `source: ./plugins/<name>` | One marketplace.json per format, listing local entries |
| **hybrid** | First-party plugins **plus** vendored third-party | `marketplace:` mixing local `./` and remote `owner/repo` | Same as monorepo, with mixed entries |

Each shape gets:
- A scaffold (`apm init --shape=<name>`).
- A canonical layout (in docs).
- A canonical release workflow (emitted by the scaffold, using `microsoft/apm-action`).
- A clear answer to "what do I tag and when."

## What's broken or missing today (G-codes)

Numbered for cross-reference. Each row says how it was verified.

### Bucket 1 — **Wrong defaults / misleading output**

- **G1. Scaffold default is a placeholder, not the user's reality.** `apm marketplace init` emits a single `acme/example-package` entry regardless of whether `plugins/` exists with real subdirs. Verified by running it on an empty repo and on a `plugins/foo/`-shaped repo: identical output. Fix: detect `plugins/` and seed the `packages:` list from it.
- **G2. Marketplace-only and monorepo shapes both produce a misleading "No plugin.json found" warning + an empty bundle directory.** Verified by running `apm pack` on a marketplace-only `apm.yml`; warning at `src/apm_cli/bundle/plugin_exporter.py:360`. The bundle path itself is not invalid — the message frames it as a missing file. **Promote to highest priority** — every marketplace-only and monorepo author hits this on their first run.
- **G3. Post-pack hint already correct (vendor-neutral) but minimal.** `pack.py:373-406` only prints "Built marketplace.json [claude] (N package(s)) -> path". No pointer to docs explaining how consumers in **any** ecosystem install the result. Fix: keep the line, append one docs link. Never name a vendor CLI.

### Bucket 2 — **Discoverability of shipped features**

- **G4. `outputs:` map form (#1317) is the new default but `apm marketplace init` still writes the deprecated list form.** Verified by inspecting `marketplace/init_template.py:89-153`. Fix: scaffold writes `outputs: {claude: {}}` map form so the next-step ("add `codex: {}`") is observable in the file.
- **G5. Per-package `tag_pattern` is supported in HEAD but appears nowhere in scaffold, docs, or `doctor` output.** Verified at `yml_schema.py:91-109`. Producers literally cannot find it without reading source. Fix: scaffold a commented `tag_pattern: "{name}-v{version}"` line under each package; document under "Per-plugin versioning"; have doctor warn when a monorepo lacks any tag_pattern (lockstep is a choice, not the only choice).
- **G6. Only two output formats** (`claude`, `codex`) are recognized; producers in the Cursor / OpenCode / Windsurf / Gemini ecosystems get an `Unknown marketplace format` error. Verified at `output_profiles.py:67-91`. Fix is a roadmap statement (which formats next, in what order), plus a public extension contract for community contributions.
- **G7. `apm marketplace doctor` is silent on the producer's two biggest concerns**: (a) which formats are configured vs. which APM supports (format coverage), and (b) whether per-package versions match git tags / lockfile (version alignment in monorepo). Add both as checks.

### Bucket 3 — **Release-time orchestration**

- **G8. `microsoft/apm-action` drops every interesting `apm pack` flag.** Verified at `apm-action/src/bundler.ts:182-192`: hardcodes `-o`, `--format`, `--target`, `--archive` only. Never passes `--marketplace`, `--marketplace-path`, `--json`, `--offline`, `--include-prerelease`. **Highest-leverage fix in this issue** — ~10 LOC unlocks multi-format CI publishing for every consumer of the action.
- **G9. No portable validators in CLI for release-time invariants.** Producers in CI need (a) "all packages share the same version" (lockstep mode) and (b) "tree is clean / committed marketplace.json matches what `apm pack` would generate now" (drift). Today they shell-script it. Add `apm pack --check-versions` and `apm pack --check-clean` as additive flags so the same checks work in GitLab/ADO/local pre-commit.
- **G10. No release-mode in `microsoft/apm-action`.** Today producers wire 6-8 release steps by hand: install, validate versions, pack each format, sha256, drift PR, release notes, upload, GH Step Summary. Verified by reading Zava's release.yml (8 steps) vs the action's surface (covers ~3). Add `mode: release` umbrella that orchestrates them, consuming `apm pack --json`.
- **G11. Codex output requires a `category:` per package** but the error fires at pack time, not at `apm marketplace doctor`. Verified by adding `outputs: {codex: {}}` to a project without categories: hard fail at pack. Fix: doctor warns; or `init --shape=…` writes a sensible `Productivity` default with a comment.

## Proposed surface

### A. Scaffold: one shape flag, four templates

Refactor the existing `apm init` surface (do **not** add a new top-level command):

```
apm init                                  # interactive: asks shape
apm init --shape=single-plugin            # current --plugin behavior
apm init --shape=marketplace-aggregator   # current --marketplace behavior, remote sources only
apm init --shape=marketplace-monorepo     # NEW: scaffolds plugins/ dir + per-package tag_pattern
apm init --shape=hybrid                   # marketplace + local + remote sources
```

Backwards compat: `--plugin` and `--marketplace` keep working, mapped to `--shape=single-plugin` / `--shape=marketplace-aggregator`, with a one-cycle deprecation note.

Every shape's scaffold writes:
- `apm.yml` with `outputs: {claude: {}}` **map form** (so `+ codex: {}` is one line away).
- A commented `tag_pattern: "{name}-v{version}"` under each package.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` that calls `microsoft/apm-action` with `mode: release` (see C below) — never raw `apm` shell.

### B. Vendor-neutral post-pack output

Replace the current minimal hint with an artifact catalog and a single docs pointer:

```
[+] Marketplace artifacts written:
    claude  -> .claude-plugin/marketplace.json   (3 packages)
    codex   -> .agents/plugins/marketplace.json  (3 packages)

[i] Consumer install patterns vary by AI assistant.
    See: https://apm.dev/docs/producer/publish-to-a-marketplace#consumers
```

This stays vendor-agnostic, scales to N formats with no string changes, and gives the docs site one URL it owns.

### C. `microsoft/apm-action` — `mode: release` umbrella

Two tracks land in apm-action and replace per-repo shell:

**C1. Pass-through fix (G8) — additive, no version bump.** Action accepts the flags `apm pack` already understands:

```yaml
- uses: microsoft/apm-action@v1
  with:
    pack: true
    marketplace: claude,codex          # → apm pack --marketplace=claude,codex
    marketplace-path: |                # → repeated --marketplace-path FORMAT=PATH
      claude=dist/claude.json
      codex=dist/codex.json
    offline: true                      # → apm pack --offline
    json-output: pack.json             # captures apm pack --json
```

**C2. Release umbrella — `mode: release`.** New input that orchestrates the canonical release flow:

```yaml
- uses: microsoft/apm-action@v1
  with:
    mode: release
    pack-each: plugins/*                 # matrix-pack each subdir; fan-in marketplace.json
    validate-versions: lockstep|per-plugin
    drift-check: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
    sha256-sidecars: true
    release-notes: from-changelog
    upload-to: github-release
```

Outputs:
```
packages: JSON array [{name, path, version, bundle, sha256}]
marketplace-drift: clean | dirty
artifacts-uploaded: N
step-summary: rendered to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY automatically
```

Internally `mode: release` shells out to the **same** `apm pack --json` it would on its own, so any maintainer can drop down to the CLI at any step.

**Open call:** the `mode:` reorg is additive in 1.x; we don't need a `v2` cut. (Maintainers, please confirm or veto.)

### D. CLI additions — narrow, portable, useful outside CI

These are the only **new CLI flags** this issue proposes. Everything richer goes in apm-action.

- `apm pack --check-versions` — fail when packages disagree (lockstep) or when any package's version doesn't match its `tag_pattern` against current `HEAD` tags.
- `apm pack --check-clean` — fail when the working tree has uncommitted changes that would alter the generated `marketplace.json`. Works in pre-commit hooks and any CI.
- `apm marketplace doctor` gains two rows:
  - **Format coverage**: "Configured: claude. Supported by APM: claude, codex. Consider adding `codex: {}` for broader reach."
  - **Version alignment**: in monorepo + per-package shapes, lists each package's version and the tag the `tag_pattern` would resolve to.

### E. Versioning answer (closes #1332)

The mechanism is already in HEAD; we just have to surface and document it.

For a marketplace-monorepo shape, producers get **two valid models**:

1. **Lockstep** (Zava's choice): every package shares one version; one `vX.Y.Z` tag per release. Default scaffold writes this.
2. **Per-package** (#1332's ask): each package has its own version; tagged independently using its `tag_pattern: "{name}-v{version}"`. Scaffold can opt into this with `apm init --shape=marketplace-monorepo --versioning=per-package`.

For Copilot CLI / Claude consumers (which today consume HEAD-of-default-branch with no version pin), this is invisible — they see the latest committed state. For APM consumers (`dependencies:` in their own `apm.yml`), the per-package tag is the pin.

This needs a docs page (`producer/versioning-strategies.md`) and three lines in `--check-versions` output, not new code.

### F. Bumping one plugin in a monorepo (closes part of #1322)

Verified empirically: bumping one plugin's `apm.yml` produces **no change** in the parent `marketplace.json` for local-source packages — the entry is `{name, description, source: ./…}` and stays a pointer. So:

- For Copilot CLI / Claude consumers: commit the bumped `plugin.json`, push to default branch. Done. They see the new version on next `marketplace update`. No tag needed.
- For APM consumers: tag `<plugin>-vX.Y.Z` with the per-package `tag_pattern`. No need to retag the whole monorepo.

`apm marketplace doctor` and `--check-versions` will both surface this so producers don't have to read source to find out.

## Acceptance criteria

A v0.14/v0.15 release that closes this issue ships:

- [ ] `apm init --shape=<single-plugin|marketplace-aggregator|marketplace-monorepo|hybrid>` (G4, A) with `--plugin`/`--marketplace` as deprecated aliases.
- [ ] Scaffold writes `outputs:` **map form** with commented `codex: {}` and a commented `tag_pattern:` (G4, G5).
- [ ] G2 (misleading "No plugin.json" warning + empty bundle dir on marketplace-only and monorepo shapes) fixed.
- [ ] G3: post-pack hint enumerates artifacts + one docs URL, names no vendor CLI (B).
- [ ] `apm marketplace doctor` adds format-coverage row and version-alignment row (G7, G11).
- [ ] `apm pack --check-versions` and `apm pack --check-clean` (D, G9).
- [ ] **`microsoft/apm-action` passes through `--marketplace`, `--marketplace-path`, `--json`, `--offline`, `--include-prerelease` (G8, C1).** This alone unblocks every CI producer today.
- [ ] **`microsoft/apm-action` ships `mode: release` orchestrating matrix-pack, drift, sha256, release notes, GH Step Summary (G10, C2).**
- [ ] Scaffolded `release.yml` uses `microsoft/apm-action@v1` with `mode: release`, never raw `apm` shell.
- [ ] Roadmap statement on next output formats (G6) with a documented contributor extension point.
- [ ] Docs: new pages `producer/repo-shapes.md`, `producer/versioning-strategies.md`; updated `publish-to-a-marketplace.md` with the consumer-paths table (B).

## Out of scope for this issue

- Adding new output formats (cursor, opencode, windsurf, gemini) — separate roadmap item per format. This issue documents the gap and the extension point.
- Marketplace-level federation / nested marketplaces.
- Signing / provenance — tracked separately.
- Anything that would name a single consumer CLI in producer-facing output.

## Open escalations (maintainer call)

These are panel disagreements I'd like ratified before implementation begins:

1. **`apm-action@v2` cut?** All proposed changes are additive in 1.x. The DevX panel and python-architect both lean "stay in v1" given the recent v1.6 default-pin precedent. Veto if you want a clean cut.
2. **Drift-PR ownership.** Three options for `mode: release` when `marketplace.json` drift is detected: (a) action embeds PR-creation logic, (b) action shells out to `peter-evans/create-pull-request`, (c) action emits the diff and exits non-zero, caller composes. Recommendation: (c) — least magic, easiest to audit.
3. **Authoritative Claude Code marketplace.json schema URL.** `yml_schema.py:725` references `json.schemastore.org/claude-code-plugin-manifest.json`; we have not fetched it. Worth confirming before we cite field names externally.
4. **Codex schema stability.** APM hardcodes `policy.installation=AVAILABLE` and `policy.authentication=ON_INSTALL` (`marketplace/output_mappers.py:236-241`) without a public Codex spec to cite. Want sign-off from the Codex side before we lean on this in scaffolds.

## References

- [#1322](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/discussions/1322) — discussion: monorepo plugin marketplace structure (jKlaus)
- [#1332](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/discussions/1332) — discussion: GitHub Releases for monorepo with per-package versions (R. Collet)
- #1281 — multi-profile marketplace outputs (the foundation)
- #1317 — marketplace output UX (filter-driven CLI + map manifest + JSON) — **shipped**
- #1318 — tracker: remove `--marketplace-output` in v0.15
- [microsoft/apm-action](https://github.com/microsoft/apm-action) — v1.6.0 (the integration point this issue extends)

issues.title: [BUG] 0.14.0: project-scope hook paths rewritten to absolute, breaking portability of checked-in .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm 0.14.0` rewrites hook `command` entries in **project-scope** `.claude/settings.json` and `.codex/hooks.json` from repo-relative to machine-absolute paths. These files are typically checked into the repo, so the absolute paths immediately break portability for every other clone/contributor/CI runner.

The change was introduced by #1354 (closes #1310). #1310 is genuinely a user-scope (`~/.claude/settings.json`) problem, but the fix was applied unconditionally and now also rewrites project-scope settings where Claude Code (and the Codex hook runner) resolve repo-relative paths just fine.

## Reproduction (using `srid/kolu`)

Kolu pins `srid/agency` as an APM dependency that ships a `Stop` hook, and checks `.claude/settings.json` and `.codex/hooks.json` into the repo.

```bash
gh repo clone srid/kolu
cd kolu
# pin apm 0.14.0 (via just recipe that wraps uvx apm-cli):
just ai::apm-update srid/agency
git diff .claude/settings.json .codex/hooks.json
```

Observed diff (paths now contain my checkout's absolute prefix):

```diff
--- a/.claude/settings.json
+++ b/.claude/settings.json
         \"hooks\": [
           {
             \"type\": \"command\",
-            \"command\": \".claude/hooks/agency/scripts/do-stop-guard.sh\"
+            \"command\": \"/Users/srid/code/kolu/.claude/hooks/agency/scripts/do-stop-guard.sh\"
           }

--- a/.codex/hooks.json
+++ b/.codex/hooks.json
         \"hooks\": [
           {
             \"type\": \"command\",
-            \"command\": \".codex/hooks/agency/scripts/do-stop-guard.sh\"
+            \"command\": \"/Users/srid/code/kolu/.codex/hooks/agency/scripts/do-stop-guard.sh\"
           }
```

A new sidecar `.claude/apm-hooks.json` also gets written with the same absolute path.

## Expected behavior

For **project-scope** settings (anything under `<repo>/.claude/`, `<repo>/.codex/`, etc. that lives inside `project_root`), `apm` should keep repo-relative paths so the generated files stay portable across checkouts, machines, and CI. The absolute-path fix from #1354 only needs to apply to **user-scope** deploys (`~/.claude/settings.json` via `apm install -g`).

## Likely fix location

`src/apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py::_rewrite_command_for_target` — currently resolves `(deploy_root / target_rel).resolve()` whenever `deploy_root` is set. The branch that calls it via `_integrate_merged_hooks` passes `deploy_root=project_root` for both user-scope and project-scope deploys. It should keep the rewrite for user-scope and skip it (or emit a path relative to `project_root`) for project-scope.

## Impact

- Generated config can't be checked in — every contributor sees a diff with their own `\$HOME` prefix.
- CI/teammates with a different checkout path get dead hooks (the absolute path doesn't exist on their machine).
- Workaround today is post-processing `.claude/settings.json` and `.codex/hooks.json` after every `apm install`/`apm deps update`.

## Environment

- apm 0.14.0 (regression from 0.13.0, which wrote repo-relative paths)
- Targets: `claude`, `codex`, `opencode`
- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.4.0); the rewrite logic is OS-agnostic so this should reproduce on Linux/Windows too.

## References

- #1354 — introducing PR (\"resolve hook paths to absolute in settings.json for --target claude\")
- #1310 — the user-scope bug #1354 was fixing
- #956 — prior \"absolute paths leak across machines\" portability bug (different surface, same class)

issues.title: [BUG] No harness detected - Copilot
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
`apm install` and `apm update` look for harness markers to detect the harness.  
For copilot, this is `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

This marker does not work if you use file-based instructions instead of always-on or compiled instructions, neither if you have agents present:
```
.apm/
    instructions/
        architecture.instructions.md
        code-conventions.instructions.md
    agents/
        my-agent.agent.md
```

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Define instructions in .apm as shown above
2. Install the package, e.g. `apm install mypackage --target copilot`
3. Run command `apm install`
4. See error

**Expected behavior**
My proposal would be to add following copilot markers:
- `.github/instructions/`
- `.github/agents/`
- `.github/prompts/`
- `.github/hooks/`

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows
 - Python Version: 3.14.3
 - APM Version: 0.14.1

**Logs**
```
$ apm install    
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
[x] No harness detected
 
APM scanned for harness markers (.claude/, CLAUDE.md, .cursor/, .cursorrules, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .codex/, .gemini/, GEMINI.md, .opencode/, .windsurf/) but found
none in this project.
 
Previously APM defaulted to copilot; this is now explicit.
 
Fix with one of:
 
  apm targets                            # see all supported harnesses
  apm install <pkg> --target claude      # deploy to a specific harness
  apm install <pkg> --target copilot     # or any supported target
 
Or declare in apm.yml:
 
  targets:
    - claude
[!] Install interrupted after 0.1s.
 
```

**Workaround**
Current workaround is specifying `--target copilot` after each install or update command.

issues.title: [BUG] apm install fails without GitLab token, but adding it directly to apm.yml succeeds
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Running `apm install git@gitlab.com:<subpath>/.../<repo>.git#<tag>` fails if there's no GitLab token available in env variables, and no git credential helper is set up.

```
Authentication failed for gitlab.com
Authentication failed for validate on gitlab.com.
No token available.
Set GITLAB_APM_PAT or GITLAB_TOKEN, or configure git 
credential fill for gitlab.com.
Run with --verbose for detailed auth diagnostics.
[!] Install interrupted after 0.8s.
```

But if I add the exact same path in apm.yml `dependencies.apm` array and run `apm install`, it works fine. It then uses my SSH key.

Occurs in GitLab SaaS for private repositories. Have not tested this with other git hosts nor public repositories.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Run command 'apm install git@gitlab.com:<subpath>/.../<repo>.git#<tag>' (private repo)
2. See error similar to above.

**Expected behavior**
Same behavior as when adding it manually to the dependencies in `apm.yml`.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS
 - Python Version: 3.12.11
 - APM Version: 0.14.2
 - VSCode Version: 1.121.0

issues.title: Converge windsurf skills onto .agents/skills/ (Cascade native cross-agent discovery)
issues.body:
## Summary

Switch the `windsurf` target's `skills` primitive deploy path from `.windsurf/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` to `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` so windsurf joins the existing 5-target convergence (copilot, cursor, codex, gemini, opencode) on the cross-tool `.agents/skills/` directory.

## Why now

The Windsurf docs explicitly endorse this. From [docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/cascade/skills#skill-scopes](https://docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/cascade/skills#skill-scopes):

> For cross-agent compatibility, Windsurf also discovers skills in `.agents/skills/` and `~/.agents/skills/`. If you have enabled Claude Code config reading, `.claude/skills/` and `~/.claude/skills/` are scanned as well.

Cascade already scans `.agents/skills/` natively at both workspace and user scope. The premise APM has been operating under -- captured verbatim in `docs/src/content/docs/producer/author-primitives/skills.md:111-113`:

> Five harnesses converge on the cross-tool `.agents/skills/` directory. Claude and Windsurf keep harness-native paths because their runtimes scan their own roots.

-- is **out of date for the windsurf half**. Cascade reads both. There is no longer a runtime reason for windsurf to stay on `.windsurf/skills/`.

## Strategic framing

APM positions itself around the [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io) spec and the cross-tool `.agents/skills/` convention (see `README.md`, `docs/.../index.mdx`, `docs/.../skills.md`). Every additional target on `.agents/skills/` strengthens that positioning and reduces per-tool duplication for multi-IDE teams (the same argument that motivated the `agent-skills` target in #1103 and the 5-target convergence).

Windsurf upstream did the work for us. APM should accept it.

## Proposed change

`src/apm_cli/integration/targets.py` -- windsurf TargetProfile:

```diff
 "windsurf": TargetProfile(
     name="windsurf",
     root_dir=".windsurf",
     primitives={
         "instructions": PrimitiveMapping("rules", ".md", "windsurf_rules"),
-        "skills": PrimitiveMapping("skills", "/SKILL.md", "skill_standard"),
+        "skills": PrimitiveMapping(
+            "skills", "/SKILL.md", "skill_standard",
+            deploy_root=".agents",   # converge per Cascade native discovery
+        ),
         "commands": PrimitiveMapping("workflows", ".md", "windsurf_workflow"),
         "hooks":    PrimitiveMapping("", "hooks.json", "windsurf_hooks"),
     },
     ...
 ),
```

(`PrimitiveMapping.deploy_root` already exists in the registry to redirect a primitive away from a target's `root_dir`; this is the same mechanism the 5 converged targets use.)

## Scope checklist

- [ ] Flip windsurf `skills` mapping to `.agents/skills/` at workspace scope
- [ ] Same flip at user scope (`~/.agents/skills/` per the Windsurf doc quote; verify `user_root_dir` interaction)
- [ ] `--legacy-skill-paths` / `APM_LEGACY_SKILL_PATHS=1` honored for windsurf (mirror the existing 5-target opt-out)
- [ ] One-time migration: uninstall stale `.windsurf/skills/<pkg>/` directories deployed by prior APM versions, or document a `rm -rf .windsurf/skills/<pkg>/` step
- [ ] Update `docs/.../author-primitives/skills.md` table (windsurf row) and the "Claude and Windsurf keep harness-native paths" sentence
- [ ] Update `packages/apm-guide/.apm/skills/apm-usage/commands.md` if it mentions the windsurf deploy path
- [ ] Add integration test pinning the new deploy path
- [ ] Add regression test that `--legacy-skill-paths` still produces `.windsurf/skills/` for windsurf
- [ ] Detection: `.agents/` is shared by multiple tools; windsurf's `detect_by_dir=True` should still key off `.windsurf/`, not `.agents/`. Verify no auto-detection regression.
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased flagged as `breaking-change` (deploy path moved) with migration note

## Sequencing

Lands **after** #1486 (which fixes the uninstall directory-collision bug under the current `.windsurf/skills/` shape; convergence builds on that fixed TargetProfile contract).

## Out of scope

- **Claude convergence onto `.agents/skills/`.** The Windsurf doc quote notes Claude scanning is opt-in via "Claude Code config reading"; not a default-on guarantee. Track separately if/when Anthropic flips the default.

## Refs

- Bug fix that unblocks this: #1486
- Original windsurf target: #1066
- 5-target convergence precedent: #1103 (`agent-skills`) and the skills.md routing table
- Windsurf docs (load-bearing citation): https://docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/cascade/skills#skill-scopes

issues.title: [BUG] LD_LIBRARY_PATH leaks bundled shared libs into git subprocesses, breaking shared-clone materialization
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
PyInstaller bootloader sets `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/apm/_internal` so the bundled Python can find `libpython3.12.so`. This leaks into every `subprocess.run()` call, including `materialize_from_bare()` in `bare_cache.py`. Bundled shared libs (libreadline.so.8, libz.so.1, libsqlite3.so.0, etc.) shadow system libraries, breaking `/bin/sh`:

```
/bin/sh: symbol lookup error: /bin/sh: undefined symbol: rl_print_keybinding
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
```

This causes `git clone --local --shared --no-checkout` to exit 128 in the shared clone cache path. The resulting user-facing error is:

```
Failed to prepare dependency from cached clone: Command git clone --local --shared --no-checkout ... returned non-zero exit status 128.
```

**To Reproduce**
1. Install APM v0.16.0 binary on an Arch Linux system
2. Create an `apm.yml` with 2+ virtual subdirectory deps from the same repo:
   ```yaml
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - owner/repo/packages/pkg-a#tag
       - owner/repo/packages/pkg-b#tag
   ```
3. Run `apm install`
4. All deps fail with exit 128

Confirm the root cause manually:
```bash
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/apm/_internal git clone --local --shared --no-checkout <bare> <dest>
# /bin/sh: symbol lookup error: ... / exit 128
```

**Expected behavior**
Virtual subdirectory dependencies from the same repo install successfully on first run.

**Environment**
- OS: Arch Linux (rolling, linux 7.0.10)
- APM Version: 0.16.0 (e94af4a)
- Git Version: 2.54.0

**Root Cause**
Two gaps in the LD_LIBRARY_PATH sanitization:

1. `git_subprocess_env()` in `git_env.py` copies `os.environ` but does not strip `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. This sanitizer exists precisely to clean ambient variables from git subprocess environments — `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` leaking is a sanitization failure.

2. `build/apm.spec` excludes only `libssl.so.3`/`libcrypto.so.3` from the bundle (fix for #462). Other bundled shared libs (libreadline.so.8, libz.so.1, liblzma.so.5, libsqlite3.so.0, libffi.so.8, libbz2.so.1.0, libuuid.so.1, libtinfo.so.6) also leak into child processes.

**Additional context**
Same class of bug as #462 (OpenSSL LD_LIBRARY_PATH leak), but broader — affects any non-Python shared library bundled by PyInstaller that differs from the system version.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-06-01
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-01
**APM Version**: 0.16.0 (f670176)
**Commands Inspected**: 29 (all required + additional subcommands discovered during inspection)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 2 |
| Low | 1 |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm mcp install --help` references a broken command

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: The help text for `apm mcp install` tells users to run `apm install --mcp --help` to see the full option list, but that invocation fails with an error.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp install --help
  ...
  Common options (see `apm install --mcp --help` for full list): --transport
  [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] ...

  $ apm install --mcp --help
  [!] Install interrupted after 0.0s.
  Error: MCP name cannot start with '-'; did you forget a value for --mcp?
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Change the guidance to `apm install --help` (which shows all `--mcp`-related flags under the main install options) or `apm mcp install --transport --help` if a narrower reference is preferred. Remove the broken `apm install --mcp --help` invocation pattern from all help text and documentation.

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm mcp install --help` — Common options displayed as unformatted paragraph

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: The "Common options" block in `apm mcp install --help` is rendered as a single squished paragraph rather than structured, indented option lines like every other command. This makes the options very difficult to read and breaks the visual consistency of the CLI.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --mcp --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
  Compare to every other command, which uses standard Click option formatting with one option per line and aligned descriptions.
- **Suggested Fix**: Replace the freeform paragraph with properly registered Click options (or an epilog section using `\n`-delimited lines). Each option should appear on its own line with standard indentation.

#### `apm config` missing `list` subcommand — inconsistent with peer command groups

- **Command**: `apm config list`
- **Problem**: Every other multi-subcommand group in APM exposes a `list` subcommand (`apm deps list`, `apm mcp list`, `apm runtime list`, `apm cache` shows `info`). `apm config` has `get`, `set`, `unset` but no `list`. Users exploring the CLI by analogy will try `apm config list` and receive an error.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config list --help
  Usage: apm config [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
  Try 'apm config --help' for help.

  Error: No such command 'list'.

  $ apm config --help
  Commands:
    get    Get a configuration value
    set    Set a configuration value
    unset  Unset a configuration value
  ```
  The bare `apm config` (no subcommand) does show a configuration table, and `apm config get` (no key) lists all keys, but neither is discoverable as `list`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a `list` alias for `apm config get` (no-arg form) so `apm config list` works and matches the pattern of peer command groups, OR document in help text that `apm config get` (with no argument) serves as the listing command.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm update` and `apm deps update` have overlapping purpose without clear differentiation in help text

- **Command**: `apm update` vs `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: Both commands update APM dependencies. The descriptions are nearly identical (`apm update`: "Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs"; `apm deps update`: "Update APM dependencies to latest refs"), and neither help text explains when to prefer one over the other. `apm install --update` was already deprecated in favor of `apm update`, suggesting consolidation is in progress, but `apm deps update` still exists as a parallel path.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm update --help
  Usage: apm update [OPTIONS]
    Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs
  Options: -y/--yes, --dry-run, -v/--verbose, -t/--target

  $ apm deps update --help
  Usage: apm deps update [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...
    Update APM dependencies to latest refs
  Options: -v/--verbose, --force, -t/--target, --parallel-downloads, -g/--global, --legacy-skill-paths
  ```
  `apm update` has `--dry-run` and `-y/--yes`; `apm deps update` has `--force`, `--parallel-downloads`, `-g/--global`. The feature sets partially overlap and are partially complementary, but there is no cross-reference in either help text.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a brief note to each command's help text explaining the relationship. For example, in `apm deps update`: "Note: prefer `apm update` for interactive upgrade planning with a confirmation prompt." Or consolidate the two commands if one is a strict superset of the other.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands passed all checks (correct formatting, no broken references, sensible error messages, consistent flag naming):

- `apm --help` — top-level help, common workflows section, correct command listing
- `apm init --help` — consistent options, deprecation notices for `--plugin` and `--marketplace` are clear
- `apm install --help` — comprehensive and well-structured despite complexity
- `apm uninstall --help` — clean and minimal
- `apm compile --help` — well-structured with clear flag semantics
- `apm run --help` — simple and correct
- `apm deps --help` (group) — lists all subcommands including `why`
- `apm deps list --help` — clean
- `apm deps tree --help` — clean
- `apm deps info --help` — clean, correct required argument behavior
- `apm deps clean --help` — clean, has `--dry-run` and `--yes`
- `apm deps why --help` — has examples, clean formatting
- `apm mcp --help` (group) — clean
- `apm mcp search --help` — clean
- `apm mcp show --help` — clean
- `apm config --help` (group) — clean, bare `apm config` correctly shows config table
- `apm config set --help` — clean
- `apm config get --help` — clean
- `apm runtime --help` (group) — clean
- `apm runtime setup --help` — clean with enum validation
- `apm runtime list --help` — clean
- `apm runtime remove --help` — clean, has `--yes`
- `apm runtime status --help` — clean
- Error behavior — all tested invalid-arg cases produce clean usage messages, no stack traces
- Documentation cross-reference — `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/config.md` correctly reflects `get`/`set`/`unset` (no false `list` reference)
