issues.title: [FEATURE] Support policy enforcement on non-GitHub remotes: add --policy to apm install (and/or auto-discovery for GitLab/ADO/plain git)
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

On non-GitHub remotes there's no way to apply policy at install time. apm install has no --policy flag, and policy auto-discovery only works for GitHub/GHE remotes.  
Both gaps are already documented in the Governance guide §14 ("Known gaps and limitations"). Per that section, when git remote get-url origin points to GitLab, ADO, or a plain git host, auto-discovery falls through with no policy applied, and the only documented mitigation is apm audit --ci --policy <path-or-url> in CI.  
That leaves a real hole: teams on a GitLab/ADO remote can gate at audit/merge time, but get zero enforcement at install time. For agent primitives, presence is effectively execution, a disallowed skill, steering file, or hook is active on the developer's workstation the moment it lands on disk, i.e. in the window between apm install and the eventual MR.   
Audit-at-merge catches it before it reaches main, but not before it reaches the developer's machine. Orgs wanting defense-in-depth (block at install, not just at review) currently have no supported mechanism on non-GitHub remotes, short of baking the policy into a custom install image, which doesn't generalize across teams.  


**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add a --policy <path-or-url> flag to apm install, mirroring the flag apm audit already supports. It would apply the policy at install time and fail closed on violation, consistent with audit behaviour.   
This is fully explicit, requires no remote detection, and lets any host (GitLab, ADO, plain git) point install at a vendored or internally-hosted policy.  
Existing semantics should be preserved: tighten-only inheritance (enterprise → org → repo), and the existing cross-host extends: rejection (credential-leak mitigation) - a vendored same-host policy is unaffected.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Extending policy auto-discovery to non-GitHub remotes (GitLab/ADO/plain git) using the same git-host abstraction already used to resolve package dependencies, which works across these hosts today. This would remove the need to pass --policy explicitly, but it's a larger surface change. Happy to go this route instead if maintainers prefer it - the --policy flag just seemed the smaller, higher-leverage fix.  
Audit-time gating only (apm audit --ci --policy …), the currently documented mitigation. This works for blocking at merge, but consciously accepts the install-to-MR workstation window with no enforcement, which is insufficient for teams that want install-time defense-in-depth.  
Baking the policy into a custom install image. Works, but every consuming team has to build and maintain their own policy-bundling image rather than pointing install at an internal policy file, not generalisable.  

**Additional context**

Both gaps are documented as known limitations in the Governance guide §14:   https://microsoft.github.io/apm/enterprise/governance-guide/#14-known-gaps-and-limitations. 
This request targets the install-time half. Related §9 air-gapped guidance already recommends apm audit --ci --policy ./vendored-policy.yml as the gating workaround, so a vendored/internally-hosted policy file is an established pattern; this just extends it to the install step.   
Motivation is enterprise rollout on an internal GitLab host where install-time enforcement is wanted alongside the existing CI gate.

A detection problem occurs when the threat detection system either:
- **Detects potential security threats** (prompt injection, secret leak, malicious patch)
- **Fails to produce results** (agent failure, parse error)

When `continue-on-error: true` (the default), these problems produce warnings and safe outputs still proceed. When `continue-on-error: false`, they block safe outputs entirely.

issues.title: [BUG] Self-defined stdio MCP env ${VAR} placeholders written verbatim instead of resolved at install time (Codex/Claude)
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

When a self-defined stdio MCP server (`registry: false`, `transport: stdio`) declares a `${VAR}` placeholder in its `env` block, targets that resolve variables at install time (Codex, Claude) write the placeholder string verbatim into the target config — even when the real value is present in `os.environ`. The MCP child process then receives an unresolved string like `MY_TOKEN=${MY_TOKEN}` and fails authentication.

On the same target, HTTP server **header** values resolve correctly. The problem is limited to the self-defined stdio **env block**.

## To Reproduce

Requirements: apm v0.23.0.

1. Create a directory with the following `apm.yml`, and create `.claude/` as the Claude target signal:

```yaml
name: repro
version: 1.0.0
dependencies:
  mcp:
    - name: env-demo
      registry: false
      transport: stdio
      command: echo
      args: ["noop"]
      env:
        MY_TOKEN: "${MY_TOKEN}"
```

2. Install with the real value in the environment:

```sh
MY_TOKEN="repro-secret-not-a-real-token" apm install --target claude
```

3. Inspect the generated `.mcp.json`:

```sh
cat .mcp.json
```

Codex behaves the same (project scope writes to `.codex/config.toml`):

```sh
MY_TOKEN="repro-secret-not-a-real-token" apm install --target codex
cat .codex/config.toml
```

## Expected behavior

`docs/.../reference/manifest-schema.md` §4.2.4 "Variable References in `headers` and `env`" normatively specifies install-time `os.environ` resolution for targets without runtime interpolation:

> **Codex, Gemini, and Cursor** have no runtime interpolation, so APM resolves `${VAR}`, `${env:VAR}`, and the legacy `<VAR>` at install time using `os.environ` (or an interactive prompt when missing).

The same table's `${VAR}` row (Codex/Gemini/Cursor column) also states "Resolved at install time from env (or interactive prompt)".

Claude is not in that table, but `src/apm_cli/adapters/client/claude.py` requires the same behaviour:

```python
# Claude Desktop / Code's mcp config does NOT support runtime env-var
# substitution -- the value in ``env`` must be a literal string. This
# adapter MUST keep the legacy install-time resolution behaviour.
_supports_runtime_env_substitution: bool = False
```

So `env: { MY_TOKEN: "${MY_TOKEN}" }` should be written resolved to the real value of `os.environ["MY_TOKEN"]`.

## Actual behavior

Claude `.mcp.json` — `MY_TOKEN` is unresolved:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "env-demo": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "echo",
      "env": { "MY_TOKEN": "${MY_TOKEN}" },
      "args": ["noop"]
    }
  }
}
```

Codex `.codex/config.toml` — identical:

```toml
[mcp_servers.env-demo.env]
MY_TOKEN = "${MY_TOKEN}"
```

For contrast, on the same Claude target, writing the value into an HTTP server header as `"Authorization": "Bearer ${MY_TOKEN}"` resolves correctly (`"Bearer repro-secret-not-a-real-token"`). This difference between the stdio env block and the header narrows down the cause.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5.1
- Python Version: runs on APM's bundled Python 3.12 build (Homebrew)
- APM Version: 0.23.0 (01b337f)
- Affected targets: codex, claude

## Additional context

Likely cause: for the self-defined stdio `env` block, the same `dep.env` dict is passed into the resolution pipeline as both the values to resolve and the `env_overrides` map. The lookup `env_overrides.get(name) or os.getenv(name)` then returns the placeholder string (truthy) and never reaches `os.getenv`, so `${MY_TOKEN}` "resolves" to itself. Header values are not keys in that map, so they fall through to `os.getenv` and resolve correctly — matching the contrast above. I can add a file/line walkthrough and a note on the test gap in a comment.

### Not a duplicate

- #1222 — Claude `.mcp.json` drops env for self-defined stdio MCP servers (the env block was emitted empty; that path now carries the env).
- #1266 — Codex/Gemini passed self-defined stdio env verbatim by *not routing it through the resolver*; that was fixed by wiring the env block through `_resolve_environment_variables`. This report is the next layer: the env block now reaches the resolver, but the resolver shadows `os.environ` with the placeholder dict, so the value is still not resolved (and the #1266 fix is what now routes Codex through that shadowing path).

issues.title: [BUG] `apm audit` reports phantom drift immediately after a clean install
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Right after a successful `apm install`, `apm audit --ci` reports several hook
files as `modified` and exits non-zero. Re-running `apm install` does not clear
it.

Capturing the audit's replay scratch tree and diffing it against disk shows the
only difference on each flagged file is the `_apm_source` ownership marker:

```diff
# .claude/apm-hooks.json  (audit replay  vs  what `apm install` wrote)
-      "_apm_source": "apm-bugs"
+      "_apm_source": "_local/apm-bugs"
```

`HookIntegrator._get_hook_source_marker()` returns `"_local/<name>"` for the
project's own root-local content and the bare `<name>` otherwise, gated on:

```python
def _is_root_local_package(package_info, project_root):
    return Path(package_info.install_path).resolve() == Path(project_root).resolve()
```

- At **install** time `project_root` is the real project dir and equals the
  self-package's `install_path` → `True` → marker `"_local/apm-bugs"`.
- During the **audit replay**, writes are redirected to a scratch dir, so the
  integrator's `project_root` is the scratch tmpdir while `install_path` still
  points at the real project → `False` → bare `"apm-bugs"`.

So the replay stamps a different marker than install did, and every hook entry
carrying `_apm_source` differs byte-for-byte from disk. Normalization
(`utils/normalization.py`) does not neutralize the marker, so it surfaces as
drift. (The one hook file with no `_apm_source` marker — the Copilot file, which
never gets one — is the only file that does *not* drift.)

**To Reproduce**
1. Install a package that deploys hooks to targets which persist `_apm_source`
   (claude, codex, cursor, gemini, windsurf): `apm install`.
2. Run `apm audit --ci`.
3. See drift reported on the just-installed files; exit code 1.

```
[!] Drift detected: 5 file(s)
  modified (5):
    - .claude/apm-hooks.json
    - .codex/hooks.json
    - .cursor/hooks.json
    - .gemini/settings.json
    - .windsurf/hooks.json
```

**Expected behavior**

A file just written by `apm install` is not reported as drifted by the next
`apm audit`. The replay should compute the same root-local marker install did
(compare `install_path` against the original project root, not the scratch
redirect target), or `_apm_source` should be excluded from the drift comparison.

**Environment**
 - OS: Linux (Arch Linux)
 - Python Version: 3.12
 - APM Version: 0.23.1

**Logs**

See the drift block above.

**Additional context**

Minimal reproduction: https://github.com/sproott/apm-bugs (`make audit`).

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-07-02
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-07-02
**APM Version**: `Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.23.1 (bf4a2b8)`
**Commands Inspected**: 51 (top-level, all subgroups: deps, mcp, config, runtime, and all standalone commands)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 4 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm doctor` has no dedicated CLI reference page

- **Command**: `apm doctor`
- **Problem**: `apm doctor` is a full command visible in `apm --help` output and referenced in 9+ documentation pages (guides, enterprise docs, reference pages for other commands), but has **no dedicated reference page** in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`. Every other non-deprecated command in `apm --help` has a corresponding `.md` file in that directory. `apm doctor` is absent.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm --help` output lists: `doctor  Run environment diagnostics (git, network, auth, gh CLI,...`
  - `ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` — no `doctor.md` file
  - Referenced in: `docs/guides/operating-installed-context.md` (x5 occurrences), `docs/enterprise/security.md`, `docs/producer/publish-to-a-marketplace.md`, `docs/reference/cli/policy.md`, `docs/reference/cli/approve.md`
  - `apm doctor --help` output: `Usage: apm doctor [OPTIONS]` with `-v, --verbose` flag
- **Suggested Fix**: Create `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md` documenting the command, its `-v/--verbose` flag, exit codes (0 = all checks pass, non-zero = critical check fails), and the list of checks it runs (git, network, auth, gh CLI, marketplace config).

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm config set/get <invalid_key>` emits a misleading "report this bug" message

- **Command**: `apm config set <invalid_key>` and `apm config get <invalid_key>`
- **Problem**: When a user provides an unknown configuration key, the CLI emits `[i] This error may indicate a bug in command routing. Please report this issue.` — a message that implies a software defect. This is a normal user-input validation path, not a bug, and will generate unnecessary bug reports.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config get invalid_key
  [x] Unknown configuration key: 'invalid_key'
  [i] Valid keys: auto-integrate, target, self-update.channel,
  self-update.install-dir, mcp-registry-url, temp-dir, allow-protocol-fallback,
  prefer-ssh
  [i] This error may indicate a bug in command routing. Please report this issue.
  ```
  Source: `src/apm_cli/commands/config.py:456-458` (config set path) and `:607-609` (config get path).
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the third `[i]` line entirely. The `[x] Unknown configuration key` and `[i] Valid keys` lines are sufficient and correct. Users should not be told to report a bug when they type an unknown key.

---

#### Reference index CLI commands table omits several documented commands

- **Command**: `docs/src/content/docs/reference/index.md`
- **Problem**: The reference index page lists CLI commands in a phase-grouped table, but the following commands have dedicated `reference/cli/*.md` pages that are not linked from the index table:
  - `approve` (and `deny`) — has `approve.md`
  - `find` — has `find.md`
  - `lock` — has `lock.md`
  - `lifecycle` — has `lifecycle.md`
  - `plugin` — has `plugin.md`
  - `publish` — has `publish.md`
  - `self-update` — has `self-update.md`
  - `doctor` — has no page (see High severity finding above)
- **Evidence**: Running `ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` shows 31 files. Cross-referencing with the index table at `docs/reference/index.md` under "CLI commands" — the above commands are absent from all phase rows.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add the missing commands to appropriate phase rows in the index table, for example:
  - Project setup: add `self-update`
  - Inspect and audit: add `find`, `lock`, `doctor`
  - Author and distribute: add `publish`, `plugin`
  - Governance: add `approve`/`deny`, `lifecycle`

---

#### `apm audit --dry-run` semantics conflict with `--dry-run` in every other command

- **Command**: `apm audit --dry-run`
- **Problem**: In every other APM command that supports `--dry-run` (`install`, `compile`, `pack`, `uninstall`, `prune`, `deps clean`, `unpack`), the flag means "preview what the whole command would do without making changes." In `apm audit`, `--dry-run` is a modifier of `--strip` only — it has no effect and emits a warning when used without `--strip`. The help text is technically accurate but the inconsistency creates a poor experience.
- **Evidence**:
  - Help text: `--dry-run   Preview what --strip would remove without modifying files`
  - Running `apm audit --dry-run` (without `--strip`) outputs: `[i] --dry-run only works with --strip (e.g. apm audit --strip --dry-run)`
  - Source: `src/apm_cli/commands/audit.py:887-889`: `if dry_run and not strip: logger.progress("--dry-run only works with --strip ...")`
  - Compare: `apm install --dry-run` help: `Show what would be installed without installing`
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) rename the flag to `--dry-strip` or `--preview-strip` so it does not conflict with the `--dry-run` convention used everywhere else, or (b) extend `--dry-run` to also preview the scan findings without writing anything (making it a true dry-run of the audit). If (a), update `audit.md` accordingly.

---

#### `apm targets --help` implies subcommands exist but none are listed

- **Command**: `apm targets --help`
- **Problem**: The usage line reads `Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...` (Click command-group syntax), which tells users there are subcommands. However, no commands are listed in the help output. `targets.md` explains this is intentional ("no subcommands ship today"), but the help text itself gives no indication — users will look for a subcommand list that simply does not appear.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm targets --help
  Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

    Show resolved targets for the current project. If APM detects a target you
    don't intend (e.g. CLAUDE.md is documentation, not a Claude Code config),
    pin your targets explicitly in apm.yml.

  Options:
    --json  Output as JSON instead of a table.
    --all   Include the agent-skills meta-target in JSON output (excluded by
            default).
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
  No "Commands:" section appears.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a note to the command description or options group, such as: `Note: no subcommands are available yet; invoking 'apm targets' without arguments prints the resolved-target table.`

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm mcp list` and `apm mcp search` have inconsistent default limits

- **Commands**: `apm mcp list`, `apm mcp search`
- **Problem**: Within the same `apm mcp` command group, `list` defaults to `--limit 20` and `search` defaults to `--limit 10`. There is no documented rationale for the difference.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm mcp list --help`: `--limit INTEGER  Number of results to show  [default: 20]`
  - `apm mcp search --help`: `--limit INTEGER  Number of results to show  [default: 10]`
- **Suggested Fix**: Align both to the same default (either 10 or 20), or document why different defaults are appropriate in the help text.

---

#### `--verbose` flag descriptions are inconsistent in detail level

- **Commands**: Multiple
- **Problem**: The `--verbose` / `-v` flag description varies from highly specific to completely generic across commands, with no consistency pattern.
- **Evidence**:
  - Generic "Show detailed output": `apm init`, `apm run`, `apm preview`, `apm doctor`
  - Contextual descriptions:
    - `apm install`: `Show detailed installation information`
    - `apm compile`: `Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis`
    - `apm update`: `Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics`
    - `apm uninstall`: `Show detailed removal information`
- **Suggested Fix**: Either standardize all descriptions to "Show detailed output" for simplicity, or give each command a contextually useful description (what *specifically* becomes visible with `--verbose`). The current mix is the worst of both worlds.

---

### Clean Areas

The following areas passed all checks with no issues:

- **Error handling**: Invalid flags, missing required arguments, and unsupported runtime values all produce clean, actionable error messages with no stack traces.
- **`--help` / `-h` flag**: Works correctly on every command and subcommand tested.
- **`--dry-run` flag**: Present and consistently described in all commands where it applies (install, compile, pack, uninstall, prune, deps clean, unpack) — except audit (see Medium finding above).
- **`-y` / `--yes` flag**: Consistent across `apm update`, `apm deps clean`, `apm runtime remove`.
- **Deprecation notices**: `apm init --plugin`, `apm init --marketplace`, `apm deps update`, and `apm unpack` all correctly show deprecation warnings with migration guidance.
- **`apm deps` subgroup**: All 7 subcommands (`list`, `tree`, `info`, `clean`, `update`, `why`, and the group itself) are consistent and properly described.
- **`apm runtime` subgroup**: All 5 subcommands (`setup`, `list`, `status`, `remove`, and the group) match the `runtime.md` documentation exactly.
- **`apm mcp` subgroup**: `search`, `show`, `install`, `list` are consistently described and match `mcp.md`.
- **`apm config` subgroup**: `get`, `set`, `unset` (and bare `apm config`) match `config.md` documentation — the `list` subcommand that was tested does not exist, which is correct per the docs.
- **Doc-to-CLI parity**: All 31 files in `docs/reference/cli/` correspond to real CLI commands. No documented command is absent from the CLI.

issues.title: [BUG] apm compile emits duplicate H1 in CLAUDE.md (extra '# Project Standards' after '# CLAUDE.md' banner); AGENTS.md has single H1
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm compile` emits **two level-1 (`#`) headings** at the top of the generated `CLAUDE.md`: the `# CLAUDE.md` banner **plus** an extra `# Project Standards` title. The Codex `AGENTS.md` produced in the same run has only a single `#` heading. This trips markdown linters (e.g. markdownlint `MD025 / single-title/single-h1`) and is inconsistent between the two output paths.

## Environment

- APM CLI: **0.23.1 (d1d926d)** (also present in 0.23.0)
- Targets: `claude`, `codex`
- OS: macOS (darwin)

## Repro

`.apm/instructions/*.instructions.md` sources contain **no** `#` (H1) headings — the highest level used is `##`:

```
$ grep -rc "^# " .apm/instructions/ | grep -v ':0'
no H1 in any source instruction
```

Run `apm compile`.

## Actual

Generated `CLAUDE.md` (two H1s):

```markdown
# CLAUDE.md
<!-- Generated by APM CLI -->
<!-- Build ID: dc755bbc9a3d -->

# Project Standards        ← extra second H1, not present in any source

## Files matching `**`
## ...
```

Generated `AGENTS.md` from the **same** compile run (single H1):

```markdown
# AGENTS.md
<!-- Generated by APM CLI from distributed .apm/ primitives -->
<!-- Build ID: 05510661a194 -->
<!-- APM Version: 0.23.0 -->

## Files matching `**`
## ...
```

So `# Project Standards` is injected **only** into the Claude output path. It is not derived from any source instruction, nor from `apm.yml` (whose `name:` is unrelated to the string "Project Standards") — it appears to be a hardcoded section title in the Claude compiler.

## Expected

The Claude output should have a single top-level `#` heading, consistent with the `AGENTS.md` output. Either:

1. Drop the extra `# Project Standards` title so `CLAUDE.md` starts with just the `# CLAUDE.md` banner followed by `##` sections (matches `AGENTS.md`), **or**
2. Demote `Project Standards` to `##` if a section title is intended.

Right now there is no CLI flag or `apm.yml` field to control this (`apm compile --help` exposes nothing for the banner/title), so users can't opt out — the double-H1 is unavoidable and, since `CLAUDE.md` is a gitignored generated artifact, it can't be hand-fixed without being overwritten on the next compile.

## Impact

- markdownlint `MD025` warnings on every generated `CLAUDE.md`.
- Inconsistency between the Claude and Codex output shapes for the same sources.

issues.title: [FEATURE] TargetProfile: plugin-bin-contract abstraction for multi-harness bin/ deployment
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Plugin `bin/` deployment is currently hard-wired to Claude Code's skills-directory plugin contract. As new harnesses adopt executable-deployment patterns (e.g. Codex CLI, Gemini CLI), each harness will need its own bin/ placement, PATH setup, and reload mechanism. Without an abstraction, the `_deploy_plugin_bin` function will grow per-harness branches and the gate logic (deny, scope, trust-posture) will be duplicated.

This was identified as item 6 in the advisory review panel on PR #1591 (tracked in #1620).

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Introduce a `TargetProfile` (or similar) abstraction that encapsulates the per-harness bin/ deployment contract:

- **bin_dir(project_root, scope)** -- where to place executables for this harness
- **bin_path_mechanism** -- how the harness discovers deployed bins (PATH env, config entry, manifest)
- **reload_hint** -- user-facing instruction to activate new executables (e.g. `/reload-plugins`, restart)
- **requires_plugin_manifest** -- whether the harness needs `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` or equivalent
- **supported_scopes** -- which install scopes (user, project) support bin/ deployment

Each `TargetProfile` would implement the contract for its harness, and `_deploy_plugin_bin` would delegate to the active profile instead of hard-coding Claude-specific logic.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Keep the current approach and add per-harness `if` branches as needed (simpler short-term, scales poorly).
- Use a registry/dict mapping harness names to deployment functions (lighter than a full class hierarchy, but less extensible).

**Additional context**

- Parent issue: #1620 (item 6)
- The current Claude-only implementation is stable and well-tested; this is a forward-looking design issue, not a regression.
- Priority: low -- only becomes relevant when a second harness adopts bin/ deployment.

issues.title: [BUG] Lockfile deployed_files records inactive-target paths from package-declared targets; audit deployed-files-present unfixable on fresh checkouts
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a dependency package declares `targets:` in its own `apm.yml` that include harnesses the consumer has NOT activated, the consumer's `apm.lock.yaml` records `deployed_files` entries for those inactive targets — but `apm install`/`apm update` (correctly) never writes them. `apm audit --ci` then fails `deployed-files-present` on any fresh checkout, permanently.

Example: `microsoft/azure-skills`, `microsoft/skills-for-copilot-studio`, and `microsoft/skills-for-fabric` declare windsurf among their package targets. A consumer with:

```yaml
targets:
- claude
- codex
- copilot
- cursor
- gemini
```

gets 67 `.windsurf/skills/...` entries in the lock's `deployed_files` (24 + 33 + 10) that never exist on disk:

```
│ deployed-files-present │ 67 deployed file(s) missing -- run 'apm install' to restore │
```

Running `apm install` does not restore them (windsurf is not an active target, so nothing writes them) — the message loops.

**To Reproduce**

1. Consumer `apm.yml` with the 5 targets above and `dependencies.apm: [microsoft/azure-skills]`.
2. `apm update --yes microsoft/azure-skills` (or `apm install` on first resolve).
3. Inspect the lock: `.windsurf/...` paths appear under the dep's `deployed_files`; no `.windsurf/` directory exists.
4. `apm audit --ci --no-fail-fast` → `deployed-files-present` fails with those paths.

Also tried: consumer-side per-dep restriction

```yaml
- git: https://github.com/microsoft/azure-skills.git
  targets: [claude, codex, copilot, cursor, gemini]
```

— fresh re-resolution still records the `.windsurf/` entries.

A likely-related symptom: the `drift` check's cache replay produces different bytes than the install write path for ~100 of the same packages' files (fabric/copilot-studio SKILL.mds), so `drift` also fails on a state that install itself just wrote. Both smell like the same root: lock/replay bookkeeping uses package-declared targets where install uses the active intersection.

**Expected behavior**

`deployed_files` in the lock should record the files actually deployed for the **active install-target intersection** (the same set install writes), so `apm audit` is self-consistent with `apm install` output on a fresh clone.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS (darwin-arm64)
- APM Version: reproduced on 0.22.0 and 0.24.0 (release binary, checksum-verified)

**Logs**

```
[>] Replaying install (cache-only)...
[!] azure-skills: filename-based target routing is deprecated.
[+] Replayed 21 package(s)
[>] Diffing scratch vs working tree...
[!] Drift detected: 110 file(s)
...
│          │ deployed-files-present   │ 67 deployed file(s) missing -- run     │
│          │                          │ 'apm install' to restore               │
[x] 2 of 9 check(s) failed
```

**Additional context**

The consumer repo gitignores `.windsurf/` (windsurf unused), so the ghost entries make every fresh checkout / CI run audit-red while the original working copy passes only when stale ignored files happen to exist. Happy to test a fix or provide the full lock excerpt.

issues.title: [BUG] A dependency's subpackage is reported as an orphan and pruned
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When an installed package's source tree contains a nested `apm.yml` (e.g. a
package that declares a dependency on a relative subpath such as
`./sub-package`, whose source lives inside it), the on-disk package scan treats
that nested directory as a **separate, top-level orphaned package**:

- `apm deps list` reports it as a direct `orphaned` project dependency.
- `apm prune` deletes it out of the installed parent package in `apm_modules/`,
  so `apm install` → `apm prune` → `apm install` oscillates forever.
- `apm audit --ci` passes throughout — its `no-orphaned-packages` check is
  lockfile-based and the nested directory has no lockfile entry — so `prune`
  and the CI gate disagree.

The nested subpackage is never actually a dependency of the consumer: the
consumer lockfile records only the parent (`./package`). It is only misreported
as one because the scan walks the filesystem into the installed package.

Root cause:
[`_scan_installed_packages()`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/commands/deps/_utils.py)
does `apm_modules_dir.rglob("*")` and returns every nested directory with an
`apm.yml`/`.apm`, without calling its sibling guard `_is_nested_under_package()`.
That guard exists, but is only wired into the
[`deps` display scan](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/commands/deps/cli.py)
and even there is gated on `has_skill_md and not has_apm_yml` — it suppresses
nested *skill* dirs only, never a nested `apm.yml`. So
[`prune`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/commands/prune.py)
`safe_rmtree`s the subdirectory as an orphan, while
[`no-orphaned-packages`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/policy/ci_checks.py)
(lockfile-based) sees nothing wrong.

**To Reproduce**
1. Have a project depend on a local `./package` whose `apm.yml` declares a
   subpath dependency (e.g. `devDependencies.apm: [./sub-package]`), with the
   source at `package/sub-package/apm.yml`.
2. Run `apm install` — installs `./package` into `apm_modules/_local/package/`;
   its `sub-package/` subfolder is copied along as part of the source.
3. Run `apm deps list`:

```
│ _local/package             │ 1.0.0   │ local    │ ... │
│ _local/package/sub-package │ 1.0.0   │ orphaned │ ... │
[!] 1 orphaned package(s) found (not in apm.yml):
[!]   - _local/package/sub-package
[i] Run 'apm prune' to remove orphaned packages
```

4. Run `apm audit --ci` — passes (`no-orphaned-packages` green), contradicting
   the list above.
5. Run `apm prune`:

```
[!] Found 1 orphaned package(s):
[!]   - _local/package/sub-package
[i] + Removed _local/package/sub-package
[*] Pruned 1 orphaned package(s)
```

   `apm_modules/_local/package/sub-package/` is now gone. The next `apm install`
   restores it; `prune` removes it again.

**Expected behavior**

A directory that lives inside an already-installed package is part of that
package, not a separate top-level dependency. `apm prune` must not delete it,
`apm deps list` must not report it as an orphan, and this must agree with what
`apm audit` reports.

**Environment**
 - OS: Linux (Arch Linux)
 - Python Version: 3.14
 - APM Version: 0.24.0

**Logs**

See the `apm deps list` and `apm prune` output above.

**Additional context**

Minimal reproduction: https://github.com/sproott/apm-bugs
(`nested-package-orphans/` — `make audit` and `make prune`).

Adjacent but distinct: #1050 (`apm compile` falsely flags the **parent**
directory of a subdirectory virtual package as orphaned) is the same
`_scan_installed_packages` scanner but the opposite topology — there the false
orphan is an *ancestor* of an expected install path, fixed by expanding expected
paths with their ancestors. Here the false orphan is a *descendant* nested
**inside** an installed package (`_local/package/sub-package`), which ancestor
expansion does not cover; the `_is_nested_under_package` guard that would suppress
it is only applied to nested skill dirs, not a nested `apm.yml`. Reproduces on
0.24.0 (after #1050's fix).

issues.title: [BUG] `apm update` does not prune orphaned MCP servers from apm.lock.yaml
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

An MCP server that is no longer declared by any dependency (or that was removed from `apm.yml`) is not removed from the `mcp_servers` / `mcp_configs` sections of `apm.lock.yaml` when running `apm update`; it lingers as an orphaned entry.

In contrast, `apm install` (and `apm install --update`) correctly prunes the same orphaned MCP server. Even though both commands re-resolve dependencies and rewrite the lockfile, `apm update` and `apm install --update` behave inconsistently.

The `apm update` command summary is "Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs", and its docstring states it will "continue the install pipeline (download + integrate + lockfile rewrite)". This implies the install pipeline — including integration (MCP integration) — runs, but in practice it does not.

## To Reproduce

1. Set up a project that depends on an APM package which transitively declares an MCP server (e.g. `foo-mcp`), and run `apm install` so that `foo-mcp` is recorded in `mcp_servers` of `apm.lock.yaml`.
2. Publish a new ref of the dependency package that no longer declares `foo-mcp` (or remove the MCP entry from `apm.yml`).
3. Run `apm update` (or `apm update -y`).
4. Inspect `apm.lock.yaml` → `foo-mcp` remains in `mcp_servers` / `mcp_configs`. No MCP-related output is printed at all.
5. Then run `apm install` → `foo-mcp` is removed from `mcp_servers` / `mcp_configs` (an MCP Servers section is printed and the orphan is pruned).

## Expected behavior

`apm update`, like `apm install`, should prune MCP servers that are no longer declared by any dependency from the `mcp_servers` / `mcp_configs` sections of `apm.lock.yaml`. At minimum, `apm update` and `apm install --update` should treat MCP servers consistently.

## Environment (please complete the following information)

- OS: macOS 26.5.2 (Build 25F84)
- Python Version: N/A (standalone binary distributed via Homebrew)
- APM Version: 0.23.1 (d1d926d)
- VSCode Version: N/A

## Logs

`apm update -y` (the side that leaves the orphan) prints no MCP-related output:

```
[>] Checking upstream for revision-pin freshness...
...
  1 updated, 5 added, 5 removed
```

`apm install` (the side that prunes) prints an MCP Servers section:

```
+- MCP Servers (2)
|  [+] deepwiki (already configured)
|  [+] redmine-mcp (already configured)
[*] All servers up to date
```

## Additional context

Inspecting the source at commit `d1d926d` (v0.23.1), the root cause is that `apm update` bypasses the install pipeline stage that performs MCP integration. A note on `apm lock` is included as well.

### Root cause analysis

MCP integration and pruning live only inside `_install_apm_packages` ([`install.py:1644`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/d1d926dc72fcaaa8563184b26351df7d7db999df/src/apm_cli/commands/install.py#L1644)).

- Orphan removal is done by `MCPIntegrator.remove_stale` ([`install.py:1936`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/d1d926dc72fcaaa8563184b26351df7d7db999df/src/apm_cli/commands/install.py#L1936)), surrounded by `collect_transitive` ([`:1855`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/d1d926dc72fcaaa8563184b26351df7d7db999df/src/apm_cli/commands/install.py#L1855)), `MCPIntegrator.install` ([`:1917`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/d1d926dc72fcaaa8563184b26351df7d7db999df/src/apm_cli/commands/install.py#L1917)), and `update_lockfile` ([`:1946`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/d1d926dc72fcaaa8563184b26351df7d7db999df/src/apm_cli/commands/install.py#L1946)).
- The lower-level function `_install_apm_dependencies` ([`install.py:2034`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/d1d926dc72fcaaa8563184b26351df7d7db999df/src/apm_cli/commands/install.py#L2034)) contains no `MCPIntegrator` calls at all. It only resolves/deploys APM packages and writes the lockfile.

Call graph:

- `apm install` → `install()` ([`install.py:1124`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/d1d926dc72fcaaa8563184b26351df7d7db999df/src/apm_cli/commands/install.py#L1124)) → `_install_apm_packages()` ([`install.py:1644`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/d1d926dc72fcaaa8563184b26351df7d7db999df/src/apm_cli/commands/install.py#L1644), contains MCP integration) → `_install_apm_dependencies()`
- `apm update` → calls `_install_apm_dependencies()` directly ([`update.py:540`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/d1d926dc72fcaaa8563184b26351df7d7db999df/src/apm_cli/commands/update.py#L540))

That is, `apm update` does not go through `_install_apm_packages` (which owns MCP integration) and instead calls the lower-level `_install_apm_dependencies` directly, so the entire MCP integration block — including `remove_stale` — never runs. The `mcp_servers` from the existing lockfile is carried forward unchanged.

Note that the `update.py` docstring ([`update.py:13`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/d1d926dc72fcaaa8563184b26351df7d7db999df/src/apm_cli/commands/update.py#L13), [`:22-23`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/d1d926dc72fcaaa8563184b26351df7d7db999df/src/apm_cli/commands/update.py#L22-L23)) states "apm update is conceptually equivalent to apm install --update" and "continue the install pipeline (download + integrate + lockfile rewrite)", so the intent is to run a pipeline that includes integration. The actual call bypasses it, so the docstring's intent and the code diverge.

### About `apm lock`

`apm lock` also calls the same lower-level `_install_apm_dependencies` directly ([`lock.py:225`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/d1d926dc72fcaaa8563184b26351df7d7db999df/src/apm_cli/commands/lock.py#L225)) and therefore does not resolve or prune MCP servers. However, this appears to be by design: the lockfile spec defines `mcp_servers` as being recorded at install time, and `apm lock` is positioned as handling package resolution only. This issue is scoped to `apm update`.

issues.title: [ARCHITECTURE] Add the OpenAPM transformation and loss-report contract
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
APM performs target-specific transformations across multiple primitives, but there is no shared machine-readable contract accounting for preserved, transformed, defaulted, dropped, or rejected fields. Loss and policy injection can therefore be silent or reported inconsistently.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Implement the reusable foundation from `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-openapm-standards-first-translation-design.md`:

- Immutable `RenderResult` accounting.
- Capability and transformation registries.
- Integration with `DiagnosticCollector` and `CommandLogger`.
- Secret-safe field-path diagnostics.
- Existing OpenAPM requirements-manifest and `tests/spec_conformance` integration.
- Golden fixtures that characterize current behavior without changing output.
- Governance preventing new unreported pairwise lossy mappings.

This foundation must remain primitive-neutral; each primitive gets its own semantic model.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Continue ad hoc diagnostics in each integrator, adopt one vendor schema as the shared pivot, or build one universal primitive IR. All three either preserve current drift or create an over-broad abstraction.

**Additional context**
Parent design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-openapm-standards-first-translation-design.md`.

This is a prerequisite for the hooks proving slice and later primitive-specific work.

issues.title: [BUG] `apm install --skill <name>` is a silent no-op when the skill is not in the plugin.json skills array
issues.body: _It's a bit of a mix-up of two different things, one is that explicit `--skill` installations do not error when said skill wasn't found. Instead the operation becomes a no-op. Which is easy to miss and leads to a confusing UX._ _The root-cause in my specific case for the skill-path not being picked up as an installable skill has to do with the repo being recognized as a Claude Plugin. Which required an agent to figure out why this behavior was happening. One improvement would be to expand the UX here, such that the user would be informed that we auto-detected the repo as a Claude Code plugin folder. Ideally we also inform them that we didn't install the skill because it didn't match the filter, optionally we can also provide the workaround command to directly install the skill and bypass the Claude Plugin install (assuming the workaround is intended to be used like this)._ _AI generated report on its findings below:_ --- **Describe the bug** Running `apm install --skill ` reports success and deploys **nothing** when `` is not exposed by the plugin's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` `skills` array. There is no warning, no error, and the exit code is 0 — the output is indistinguishable from a successful install, which makes the failure very hard to diagnose. The `--skill` feature itself works; the only broken case is requesting a skill that the plugin manifest does not expose. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Run command `apm install -v mattpocock/skills --skill engineering/resolving-merge-conflicts --target claude` 2. `skills/engineering/resolving-merge-conflicts/SKILL.md` **exists** in the source repo (https://github.com/mattpocock/skills), so a skill is expected to be deployed. 3. See that `.claude/skills/` is empty and no diagnostic is printed. Confirmation matrix (same repo, same command shape, only `--skill` value varies): | `--skill` value | Listed in plugin.json? | Skills deployed | |---|---|---| | `engineering/tdd` | yes | 1 ✅ | | `tdd` | yes | 1 ✅ | | `engineering/resolving-merge-conflicts` | no | 0 ❌ (silent) | | `resolving-merge-conflicts` | no | 0 ❌ (silent) | | _(bare install, no `--skill`)_ | — | 21 ✅ | **Expected behavior** When a `--skill` filter matches zero available skills, APM should say so and list what *is* available, e.g.: ``` --skill matched no skills in 'skills'. Requested: engineering/resolving-merge-conflicts. Available: ask-matt, code-review, ..., tdd, teach, ..., writing-great-skills. A skill that exists in the source repo but is missing here is not declared in the package's plugin.json. ``` Deployment behavior need not change — only the missing diagnostic. **Environment (please complete the following information):** - OS: macOS 26.5.2 - Python Version: bundled interpreter (Homebrew-distributed `apm` binary) - APM Version: 0.23.1 (d1d926d) - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A **Logs** Actual output of the failing command (trimmed): ``` [+] mattpocock/skills @e4722b8e |-- (files unchanged) ... [*] Installed 1 APM dependency in 1.0s. ``` `.claude/skills/` is empty afterwards; exit code 0. **Additional context** *Root cause.* `mattpocock/skills` is detected as a MARKETPLACE_PLUGIN because it ships `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, which declares an explicit `skills` array of 21 paths. At install time, `plugin_parser.py` treats a `skills` array as a path-remap allowlist (`_resolve_sources("skills", "skills")`, `src/apm_cli/deps/plugin_parser.py:736-768`): only the listed directories are copied into `.apm/skills/` and then promoted to `.claude/skills/`. `engineering/resolving-merge-conflicts` is not in that array, so it never lands in `.apm/skills/` and the `--skill` filter has nothing to match. The filter miss is swallowed silently — `_promote_sub_skills` just `continue`s past non-matching entries (`src/apm_cli/integration/skill_integrator.py:673`) and no caller checks whether the requested subset matched anything. *Suggested fix.* Emit a warning (listing available skill names) when a `--skill` filter matches zero skills, in `_promote_sub_skills_standalone` and `_integrate_skill_bundle` in `skill_integrator.py`. This mirrors the existing `--skill filter ignored for single CLAUDE_SKILL` warning precedent (`skill_integrator.py:1337`) and does not change what gets deployed. *Workaround.* Install the skill directly by its subdirectory path, bypassing the manifest — it resolves as a standalone `CLAUDE_SKILL`: ``` apm install mattpocock/skills/skills/engineering/resolving-merge-conflicts --target claude ``` *Possibly a separate issue.* There is an internal tension worth flagging: `apm pack` treats `agents`/`skills`/`commands` keys in `plugin.json` as schema-invalid and strips them (`plugin_exporter.py:374`, per the official Claude Code plugin schema — convention dirs are auto-discovered, not listed), but the install side (`plugin_parser.py`) still honors those same keys as a path-remap allowlist. So a hand-authored `plugin.json` that lists convention-dir paths silently narrows what is installable, which is exactly what bit this repo. Whether the install side should ignore convention-dir `skills` entries and fall back to auto-discovery is a design question separate from the silent-no-op bug above.

issues.title: [BUG] Generated GitHub Copilot hook JSON omits the required top-level version: 1 field
issues.body:
## Summary

When `apm` generates GitHub Copilot hook files (`.github/hooks/*.json`) from a
manifest that does not declare an explicit version, the emitted JSON omits the
required top-level `version` field, producing `{ "hooks": { ... } }` instead of
`{ "version": 1, "hooks": { ... } }`. The official GitHub Copilot hooks format
**requires** a top-level `version` of `1`, so APM-deployed Copilot hooks are
non-conformant unless the source manifest happens to carry a version.

## Baseline and environments

- Baseline SHA: `4257698916736679478af4a9c37dc055b22b0d7a` (origin/main)
- APM: 0.24.1 (`uv run apm`)
- Platform / arch: macOS / arm64
- Harness: GitHub Copilot (hook target); Claude Code used only for isolation
  control.

## Native contract

Official GitHub Copilot hooks documentation (accessed 2026-07-10), two sources:

- `https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/hooks` -- "Hook
  configuration format": *"The JSON must contain a `version` field with a value
  of `1` and a `hooks` object containing arrays of hook definitions."* The
  documented example is `{ "version": 1, "hooks": { ... } }`.
- `https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference` -- hook
  configuration files use JSON format with version `1`.

## Exact reproduction

```
# disposable project with a version-absent hook primitive
uv run apm install --target copilot,claude
uv run apm compile --target copilot,claude --force-instructions
# inspect generated .github/hooks/*.json
```

Generated Copilot hook (baseline, version-absent input):

```json
{ "hooks": { "sessionStart": [ { "type": "command", "bash": "..." } ] } }
```

Required by contract:

```json
{ "version": 1, "hooks": { "sessionStart": [ { "type": "command", "bash": "..." } ] } }
```

## Expected and actual behavior

- Expected: every generated `.github/hooks/*.json` carries top-level
  `version: 1` and native camelCase events; Claude output stays isolated.
- Actual: two fresh version-absent inputs emitted only `hooks` at top level
  (no `version`), failing native validation. A source `version=1` control
  preserved the field; Claude/Copilot target isolation held.

## Finder and independent confirmation

- Finder: `nhf-w3-macos`.
- Confirmer: `conf-nhf-r1-03` (distinct identity). Independently reproduced APM
  output AND live-fetched the official Copilot doc to verify the version
  requirement is real. Confidence high. (This candidate was explicitly
  re-checked for false-positive risk; the official contract confirms the
  requirement.)

## Falsification controls

- Source manifest with explicit `version=1` preserved the field and passed
  native validation -> the omission is specific to version-absent input.
- Claude settings retained only `SessionStart` while Copilot retained only
  `sessionStart` -> target isolation intact; not a cross-target leak.

## Normalized fingerprint

`COPILOT_HOOK:REQUIRED_VERSION_1_OMITTED`

## Historical siblings

- OPEN #2071 Kiro hook integrator emits legacy pre-1.0 hook schema.
- OPEN #2062 `apm install --target claude` writes flat hook entries (missing
  matcher/hooks nesting).
- CLOSED #2020 combined hook manifests route to one target only; claude
  silently gets Copilot-schema fallback hooks.
- Related epic #2112 (replace vendor-to-vendor translation with OpenAPM
  semantic models), #2031.

## Architecture diagnosis

`src/apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py` injects a top-level version default
(`top_level_defaults={"version":1}`) only for the cursor/codex merge targets
(`_MERGE_HOOK_TARGETS`). Copilot is not in that map and is emitted through a
separate copied-file path that bypasses `top_level_defaults`, so every
version-absent Copilot hook payload lacks the required field. This is one more
instance of per-harness hook-schema divergence in `hook_integrator.py` (see
sibling cluster above).

## Blast matrix

- command: `install`, `compile`
- scope: project (`.github/hooks/`), and Copilot personal `~/.copilot/hooks/`
- primitive: hooks
- target: copilot (defect); cursor/codex carry version; claude/kiro tracked
  separately
- host: n/a
- platform: platform-independent

## Fix constraints

Minimal remediation: ensure the Copilot hook emission path applies the required
top-level `version: 1` default (consistent with the native Copilot contract)
when the source manifest omits it, without a harness translation layer -- this
is honoring the native Copilot primitive contract, not translating between
harnesses. Add a regression test asserting generated Copilot hook JSON always
has top-level `version: 1`. Fix/TDD/CI ownership: `batch-bug-shepherd`.

## Principles

- Native-fidelity: emitted primitives must satisfy the official upstream
  (Copilot) schema.
- Vendor-neutral: fix stays within the native Copilot contract; no cross-vendor
  translation layer.

## Evidence

Finder (two reproductions + version-present and target-isolation controls) and
confirmer artifacts (including the live official-contract capture) are archived
by the red-team run. Full sanitized artifacts available on request.

---
Filed by the APM red-team reliability sweep (Round 1). The official Copilot
contract was live-verified during confirmation. Handed to `batch-bug-shepherd`
for triage, TDD, review, CI, and mergeability.

issues.title: [BUG] Uninstalling the last-writer of a shared deployed file drops lockfile ownership from the surviving package (content-integrity coverage silently lost until reinstall)
issues.body:
## Summary
When two installed packages deploy the *same* file (a shared deployed path, e.g. an identical `*.instructions.md`), APM assigns lockfile ownership of that path to a single "last-writer" package. Uninstalling that last-writer correctly leaves the file on disk (a surviving package still provides it) and re-integrates the surviving package -- but it never transfers the `deployed_files` / `deployed_file_hashes` ownership rows to the surviving package. The shared file becomes lockfile-orphaned: present on disk, but no lockfile entry claims it, so `content-integrity` (and `apm audit --ci --no-drift`) stops verifying it until the next `apm install` restores ownership.

## Impact
- After a routine uninstall, a still-required shared file silently drops out of content-integrity coverage. Under `apm audit --ci --no-drift` (the documented reduced-coverage CI mode), tampering with that file is no longer detected (exit 0) where the unique-path control correctly detects it (exit 1).
- Self-heals on the next `apm install`, so this is a bookkeeping / coverage gap rather than data loss.

## Reproduction (Round 3 reliability sweep; finder + independent confirmer both reproduced)
1. Create two local packages A and B that each contain an identical `shared.instructions.md`.
2. `apm install` (root depends on both), then `apm update` and `apm compile`.
3. `apm uninstall <B>` (the last-writer owner of the shared path).
4. Observe: A and the integrated file remain on disk, but A has no `deployed_files` row for the shared path.
5. Tamper with the shared file; `apm audit --ci --no-drift` exits `0` (a distinct-paths control exits `1`).
6. `apm install` restores ownership; audit again detects tampering.

## Root cause (canonical-owner gap)
`apm install` has a last-writer reconciler that assigns shared-path ownership; `apm uninstall` has no counterpart. In `src/apm_cli/commands/uninstall/cli.py` the removal set `all_deployed_files` is computed solely from the *removed* packages' `deployed_files`, the lockfile update only deletes removed keys, and nothing re-assigns a surviving co-owner's ownership of a shared path. The "who owns this deployed path" fact is written by one entry path (install) and never reconciled by its sibling (uninstall).

## Expected
After uninstalling a shared path's last-writer, ownership (`deployed_files` + `deployed_file_hashes`) should transfer to a surviving package that still provides that path, keeping content-integrity coverage intact without requiring a reinstall.

## Strategy compliance
Native Copilot instruction Markdown throughout; the fix is lockfile bookkeeping (ownership handoff), not harness translation. Vendor-neutral.

issues.title: Make uninstall deployment-state persistence atomic
issues.body:
Uninstall persists dependency removal before ledger reconciliation, so an interruption can leave the lockfile internally inconsistent (records owned by a deleted dependency). Reconcile dependency removal, survivor handoff, hashes, and ledger in memory, then perform one durable lockfile write. No demonstrated regression today; this hardens the failure window.

---
Surfaced by the advisory review panel on #2155 and deferred as out-of-scope for that consolidation PR. Filed for tracking by the reliability campaign.

issues.title: [BUG] Codex target silently drops agent MCP tool scope
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

APM 0.25.0 silently drops an agent's `tools:` restriction when compiling the
agent for the Codex target.

APM installs all declared MCP servers into the project `.codex/config.toml`, but
the generated `.codex/agents/<agent>.toml` contains only `name`, `description`,
and `developer_instructions`. It contains no per-agent `mcp_servers`, `enabled`,
or `enabled_tools` configuration, and APM emits no warning that the restriction
was discarded.

Codex custom-agent configuration supports `mcp_servers`, and omitted optional
fields inherit from the parent session. Therefore an agent intended to use only
one MCP server can inherit every project/session MCP server instead.

Codex documentation:

- https://developers.openai.com/codex/subagents/
- https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference/

## Minimal reproduction

Create `apm.yml`:

```yaml
name: apm-codex-agent-scoping-repro
version: 0.1.0
targets:
  - codex
dependencies:
  apm: []
  mcp:
    - name: allowed-demo
      registry: false
      transport: stdio
      command: npx
      args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"]
    - name: unlisted-demo
      registry: false
      transport: stdio
      command: npx
      args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"]
includes: auto
scripts: {}
```

Create `.apm/agents/scoped-reviewer.agent.md`:

```markdown
---
name: scoped-reviewer
description: Minimal reproduction for Codex per-agent MCP tool scoping.
tools: [read, search, 'allowed-demo/*']
---

Review the requested change and report concrete findings.
```

Run:

```powershell
uvx --from 'apm-cli==0.25.0' apm install --target codex --verbose
```

## Actual behavior

APM writes both servers to `.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.allowed-demo]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"]

[mcp_servers.unlisted-demo]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"]
```

But `.codex/agents/scoped-reviewer.toml` contains only:

```toml
name = "scoped-reviewer"
description = "Minimal reproduction for Codex per-agent MCP tool scoping."
developer_instructions = "Review the requested change and report concrete findings."
```

There is no `mcp_servers`, `enabled`, or `enabled_tools` entry. The `tools:`
restriction is silently lost.

## Expected behavior

For MCP-qualified tool entries, APM should either:

1. generate valid per-agent Codex MCP configuration, including the complete
   transport definitions required by the custom-agent config layer, so only
   declared servers/tools are exposed; or
2. emit a clear lossy-compilation warning identifying the agent and discarded
   field.

Silently widening tool access is unsafe.

## Additional validation

In a separate runtime check with Codex CLI 0.144.1:

- structurally valid custom-agent TOML files were discovered and invoked
  successfully;
- partial agent MCP tables containing only `enabled = false` were rejected as an
  invalid transport;
- complete MCP transport definitions plus `enabled = true/false` were accepted;
  and
- the resulting allow/deny behavior was enforced.

This supports the hypothesis that the gap is in APM's Codex output generation,
not Codex custom-agent discovery.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- APM CLI: 0.25.0
- Codex CLI: 0.144.1

## Related issues

- #293
- #581

issues.title: [BUG] `apm outdated` / `apm update` report `unknown` for Azure DevOps deps — `LockedDependency.to_dependency_ref()` drops `ado_*` fields (distinct from #2150 / #2119)
issues.body:
### Summary

On **v0.25.0** (which already includes the ADO auth fixes from #2150 and #2119), `apm outdated` still reports `unknown` for every Azure DevOps dependency, and `apm update` cannot resolve semver ranges against ADO. This is **not** the auth-scheme issue from #2150 nor the URL-suffix issue from #2119 — both of those are fixed in this build.

Root cause: `LockedDependency.to_dependency_ref()` rebuilds a `DependencyReference` from the lockfile **without** the ADO coordinate fields (`ado_organization`, `ado_project`, `ado_repo`). The rebuilt ref reports `is_azure_devops() == True` (host-only check) but those fields are `None`, so `to_github_url()` calls `urllib.parse.quote(None)` → `TypeError`. The exception is swallowed by the `except Exception:` handlers in the outdated/update paths, degrading the result to `unknown`.

### Key distinguishing evidence (rules out #2150 / #2119)

On the **same** v0.25.0 install with an active `az login` session (no `ADO_APM_PAT` set):

- ✅ `apm view "dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/{repo}" versions` — **works**, lists `v1.0.0`, `v1.1.0`, etc. (builds the ref via `DependencyReference.parse()`, which populates `ado_*`).
- ✅ `git ls-remote` against the same repo — works.
- ❌ `apm outdated` — `unknown`, with an **empty Source column**.
- ❌ `apm update` (with `ref: ^1.0.0`) — resolves to `-` and prints "No dependency changes were applied".

If this were an auth problem (#2150 / #2119), `apm view versions` and `git ls-remote` would fail too. They don't — so the difference is purely how the dependency reference is reconstructed: `view` uses `parse()` (populates `ado_*`), while `outdated`/`update` use `to_dependency_ref()` (leaves `ado_*` as `None`).

### Environment

- APM version: `0.25.0` (build includes #2121 and #2155)
- Host: Azure DevOps (`dev.azure.com`); auth via `az login` bearer; `ADO_APM_PAT` unset
- OS: Windows

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add an Azure DevOps dependency pinned to a semver tag, e.g. `dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/{repo}#v1.0.0`, where the repo has annotated tags `v1.0.0` and `v1.1.0`.
2. `apm install` (writes a lockfile entry with `host: dev.azure.com`, `repo_url: {org}/{project}/{repo}`, `resolved_ref: v1.0.0`).
3. Run `apm outdated`.

### Actual output

```
┃ Package               ┃ Current ┃ Latest ┃ Status  ┃ Source ┃
│ dev.azure.com/{org}/… │ v1.0.0  │ -      │ unknown │        │
[i] Some dependencies could not be checked (branch/commit refs)
```

The **empty Source column** is diagnostic: the check exited via the early `except` path (which builds an `OutdatedRow` without `source=`), not the tag-comparison path (which sets `source="git tags"`).

`apm update` with a `ref: ^1.0.0` range shows:

```
[~] {org}/{project}/{repo}
    ref: v1.0.0 -> ^1.0.0 (f2dee13 -> -)
  No dependency changes were applied.
```

The `-` (resolved commit) confirms the range resolved to nothing.

### Expected behavior

`apm outdated` should report `Latest = v1.1.0`, `Status = outdated`, `Source = git tags`, and `apm update` should resolve `^1.0.0` to `v1.1.0` — exactly as `apm view versions` already does for the same repo.

### Root cause analysis

**1. `LockedDependency.to_dependency_ref()`** — `src/apm_cli/deps/lockfile.py` (~L588–620) — copies `repo_url` / `host` but never sets the ADO fields, so they default to `None`:

```python
def to_dependency_ref(self) -> DependencyReference:
    ...
    return DependencyReference(
        repo_url=self.repo_url,
        host=self.host,
        host_type=self.host_type,
        port=self.port,
        reference=ref,
        virtual_path=self.virtual_path,
        is_virtual=self.is_virtual,
        artifactory_prefix=self.registry_prefix,
        ...
        # ado_organization / ado_project / ado_repo NOT set → None
    )
```

**2. `is_azure_devops()`** — `src/apm_cli/models/dependency/reference.py` — is host-only:

```python
def is_azure_devops(self) -> bool:
    return self.host is not None and is_azure_devops_hostname(self.host)
```

**3. `to_github_url()`** — `src/apm_cli/models/dependency/reference.py` (~L2039) — builds the ADO URL exclusively from the (now `None`) fields:

```python
if self.is_azure_devops():
    project = urllib.parse.quote(self.ado_project, safe="")  # None → TypeError
    repo    = urllib.parse.quote(self.ado_repo, safe="")
    return f"https://{netloc}/{self.ado_organization}/{project}/_git/{repo}"
```

`urllib.parse.quote(None)` raises `TypeError`.

**4. Swallowed** — `src/apm_cli/commands/outdated.py::_check_one_dep`:

```python
try:
    remote_refs = downloader.list_remote_refs(dep_ref)
except Exception:
    return OutdatedRow(package=package_name, current=..., latest="-", status="unknown")  # no source=
```

The same failure occurs in the semver `resolve()` path used by `apm update` (`src/apm_cli/deps/git_reference_resolver.py`), where `list_remote_refs()` throws and the range resolves to nothing.

### Why existing tests miss it

`tests/unit/test_outdated_command.py::test_ado_dep_builds_correct_reference` fully mocks the downloader (`mock_downloader.list_remote_refs.return_value = [...]`), so it never constructs a real ADO URL and never hits `quote(None)`. It only asserts `list_remote_refs.assert_called_once()`. The test's docstring says ADO deps "should pass full URL to `DependencyReference.parse()`," but the actual code path calls `to_dependency_ref()`, not `parse()` — so the real URL construction is untested.

### Suggested fix

- Repopulate the ADO coordinates in `LockedDependency.to_dependency_ref()` — derive `ado_organization` / `ado_project` / `ado_repo` by splitting `repo_url` (`org/project/repo`) when the host is Azure DevOps.
- Additionally harden `to_github_url()` to fall back to splitting `repo_url` when the ADO fields are `None`, so a partially-populated ADO ref can never crash the URL builder.
- Add a regression test that exercises the **real** (non-mocked) ADO URL construction from a lockfile-rebuilt ref.

### Related (already fixed, different root cause)

- #2150 — semver install/update dropped the ADO bearer auth scheme (`install/helpers/ref_reuse.py`).
- #2119 — ADO marketplace `sourceBase` `.git` suffix + az-bearer fallback.

Both were fixed in v0.25.0; this report is a separate defect in the lockfile-rebuild path.

issues.title: [BUG] config-consistency requires apm.yml for is_virtual packages (regression in 0.25.0)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Since v0.25.0, the `config-consistency` baseline check (run by `apm audit --ci`) fails for every dependency that APM itself marks `is_virtual: true` in the lockfile (a `git:` + `path:` skill pointing at a sub-directory, `package_type: claude_skill`).

The new `src/apm_cli/integration/mcp_config_view.py` (added in commit `0c56ce31`, PR #2155) requires an `apm.yml` package manifest on disk for each locked dependency, and exempts **only** `package_type == "skill_bundle"`:

```python
# src/apm_cli/integration/mcp_config_view.py
if not manifest_path.exists():
    if dependency.package_type == "skill_bundle":
        continue
    problems.append(
        McpSourceProblem(
            package_key=package_key,
            manifest_path=manifest_path,
            message=(
                f"package manifest not found at {manifest_path}; "
                "re-run 'apm install' to restore it"
            ),
        )
    )
    continue
```

Virtual packages have no `apm.yml` of their own by definition, and `apm install` never deploys one for them, so the check can never be satisfied. `apm install` and this check are inconsistent with each other: install (0.25.0) produces zero `apm.yml` files under `apm_modules/` for these packages, yet the check demands one.

The exemption ignores the `is_virtual` flag, even though `LockedDependency` exposes it (`is_virtual: bool = False` in `src/apm_cli/deps/lockfile.py`). In v0.24.0 the check did not scan per-dependency manifest presence at all (the message "package manifest not found" does not exist anywhere in the 0.24.0 source), so this is a regression introduced by the 0.25.0 refactor.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. In a project `apm.yml`, declare at least one skill dependency as a sub-directory of a repo, e.g.:
   ```yaml
   dependencies:
     apm:
     - git: angular/skills
       path: angular-developer
       targets: [claude]
     - git: microsoft/playwright-cli
       path: skills/playwright-cli
       targets: [claude]
   ```
2. Run `apm install` (APM 0.25.0). The lockfile records these as `is_virtual: true`, `package_type: claude_skill`. No `apm.yml` is written under `apm_modules/.../` for them (`find apm_modules -name apm.yml` returns nothing).
3. Run `apm audit --ci`.
4. See `config-consistency` fail:
   ```
   config-consistency | N MCP config inconsistenc(ies) -- run 'apm install' to reconcile
     - angular/skills/angular-developer: package manifest not found at
       .../apm_modules/angular/skills/angular-developer/apm.yml; re-run 'apm install' to restore it
     - microsoft/playwright-cli/skills/playwright-cli: package manifest not found at
       .../apm_modules/microsoft/playwright-cli/skills/playwright-cli/apm.yml; re-run 'apm install' to restore it
   [x] 1 of 7 check(s) failed
   ```
   Re-running `apm install` does not help (nothing produces the missing `apm.yml`). A sibling `skill_bundle` dependency in the same project passes because it is exempted.

**Expected behavior**
`config-consistency` should not require an `apm.yml` for packages APM itself flagged `is_virtual: true` — they have no manifest by design and `apm install` never deploys one. The missing-manifest exemption should cover virtual packages as well as `skill_bundle`, e.g.:

```python
if dependency.package_type == "skill_bundle" or dependency.is_virtual:
    continue
```

`apm audit --ci` should pass for a project whose only "problem" is virtual, path-based skill dependencies.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux (GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`) and Windows 11 — reproduced on both
 - Python Version: 3.14.6 (local); GitHub-hosted runner Python on CI
 - APM Version: 0.25.0
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): n/a

**Logs**
```
                           APM Policy Compliance
 config-consistency | 5 MCP config inconsistenc(ies) -- run 'apm install' to reconcile
 drift              | drift skipped: install cache not populated (run 'apm install' first or pass --no-drift)

  config-consistency details:
    - angular/skills/angular-developer: package manifest not found at
      /home/runner/work/.../apm_modules/angular/skills/angular-developer/apm.yml; re-run 'apm install' to restore it
    - luccasa/ai-tools/globals/skills/front/ngrx-signals: package manifest not found at ...
    - luccasa/ai-tools/globals/skills/front/ui/accessibility: package manifest not found at ...
    - luccasa/lucca-front/.github/skills/lucca-front/lucca-front-21-2-5: package manifest not found at ...
    - microsoft/playwright-cli/skills/playwright-cli: package manifest not found at ...

[x] 1 of 7 check(s) failed
```

**Additional context**
- Introduced in commit `0c56ce31` (`refactor(core): consolidate red-team lifecycle fixes behind canonical owners`, #2155), released in v0.25.0.
- Relevant code: `src/apm_cli/integration/mcp_config_view.py` (`_collect_locked_dependencies`); flag defined in `src/apm_cli/deps/lockfile.py` (`LockedDependency.is_virtual`).
- Impact: any project using `git:`+`path:` (sub-directory) skill dependencies — a common pattern — has a permanently red `apm audit --ci` gate on 0.25.0, with no user-side remediation (the referenced `apm install` fix does not produce the required file, and third-party source repos such as `angular/skills` and `microsoft/playwright-cli` cannot be given an `apm.yml`).
- A PR implementing the one-line exemption fix follows.

issues.title: [BUG] apm prune leaves orphaned hook entries in merged configs (settings.json / apm-hooks.json)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm prune` removes an orphaned package's directory and its lockfile-tracked `deployed_files`, but never unmerges the package's hook entries from merged-hook configs (`.claude/settings.json` + the `apm-hooks.json` ownership sidecar, `.cursor/hooks.json`, etc.).

`apm uninstall` handles this correctly: `commands/uninstall/engine.py` calls `HookIntegrator.sync_integration()`, which runs `_clean_apm_entries_from_json()` to filter out entries owned via `_apm_source` markers (re-injected from the sidecar for schema-strict targets like Claude).

`commands/prune.py` never calls into that path — it only does `safe_rmtree()` on the package dir plus per-file `deployed_files` cleanup. Merged JSON entries are not in `deployed_files` (they're merged *into* a shared file), so they survive the prune.

The result is dead hook wiring: Claude Code fires every configured hook and logs a `PreToolUse:Bash hook error … No such file or directory` on each tool call, for every pruned package that had merged hooks.

**To Reproduce**

1. In a project (or user scope), install a package that ships hooks (entries get merged into `.claude/settings.json`, ownership recorded in `.claude/apm-hooks.json`).
2. Remove the package from `apm.yml`.
3. Run `apm prune` — the package dir under `apm_modules/` and its `.claude/hooks/<pkg>/` scripts are removed.
4. Inspect `.claude/settings.json` / `.claude/apm-hooks.json`: the package's hook entries are still present, pointing at the deleted scripts.
5. Any Claude Code session now emits `hook error: No such file or directory` on every matching event.

**Expected behavior**

`apm prune` should behave like `apm uninstall` for integration cleanup: after removing orphaned package dirs, run the same `sync_integration()` / `_clean_apm_entries_from_json()` pass so merged hook entries owned by the pruned packages are removed from all merge-based targets and their sidecar markers.

A related (smaller) gap: on package *upgrade*, the hook integrator only adds/updates merged entries. If a new package version drops a hook script that an older version declared, the old merged entry survives and points at a now-deleted file. A reconciliation pass ("remove entries whose `_apm_source` package no longer declares them") would close both holes.

**Environment**
 - OS: macOS (darwin 25.3)
 - Python Version: 3.13
 - APM Version: 0.24.1 and 0.25.0 (code inspected in both)

**Logs**

```
PreToolUse:Bash hook error
Failed with non-blocking status code: /bin/sh: ~/.claude/hooks/hooks-git-workflow/scripts/pre-push-test-gate.sh: No such file or directory
```

(repeated on every Bash tool call after pruning the owning package)

issues.title: Formalize a spec requirement for uninstall reachability preservation (req-lk-0XX)
issues.body:
## Context

PR #2269 fixes a confirmed defect: `apm uninstall` deleted a shared transitive dependency (`_local/shared`) still declared/reachable by a surviving direct dependency, because `LockedDependency.resolved_by` is single-valued (first-wins) and `commands/uninstall/engine.py::_build_children_index()` used it as an implicit (and here wrong) reachability oracle.

The fix adds `src/apm_cli/deps/reachability.py` (~245 lines): an additive, read-only forward-reachability walker from surviving direct dependencies, used by uninstall to decide what a candidate orphan may safely keep. No lockfile schema change; `resolved_by`/`local_path` stay `str | None` (repaired in place when a rescue changes which parent legitimately anchors a still-reachable entry, never widened to multi-parent storage).

## Why this issue exists

The repo's Mode B "silent-extension" spec-conformance gate (`tests/spec_conformance/mode_b_detector.sh`) flags `src/apm_cli/deps/` as a normative OpenAPM v0.1 critical path ("resolver"). PR #2269 lands substantive new behavior there without a corresponding spec anchor, so it was shipped with an explicit `apm-spec-waiver:` per `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s "Mode B (silent extension)" guidance -- this is a genuine bug fix restoring intended/expected uninstall behavior, not a new user-facing capability, and CONTRIBUTING.md documents the waiver mechanism for exactly this class of change ("true refactor / perf rewrite / internal cleanup with no observable behaviour delta" is the literal text, though this fix does have an observable behavior delta in the sense that it corrects a bug -- see PR discussion for the full judgment call).

The existing `req-lk-020` (added in spec v0.1.13, per the spec's own changelog table) already covers an adjacent but narrower case: *"the consumer MUST preserve any path freshly deployed by an active dependency in the current install, even when the same path is also recorded by a prior lockfile entry under a different dependency identity"* (deployed-file reconciliation during install). It does **not** explicitly cover the case this PR fixes: a transitive **lockfile dependency entry** (not just a deployed file path) that remains reachable from a surviving declared parent must not be removed during `uninstall`'s orphan-cleanup pass, even when its recorded `resolved_by` names a package that was just removed.

## Ask

Author a proper OpenAPM v0.1 requirement (likely `req-lk-021` or the next free `req-lk-0XX`) documenting:

1. During uninstall-time orphan cleanup, a conforming consumer implementation MUST NOT remove a transitive dependency lockfile entry that remains reachable (via forward reachability from the manifest's surviving declared dependencies) even though its recorded `resolved_by` names a package being removed in the same operation.
2. When such an entry is rescued, its `resolved_by` (and, for local deps, `local_path`) MUST be repaired to name a still-valid surviving parent, since a stale anchor would otherwise silently corrupt the entry's resolvability on a later uninstall.
3. If reachability cannot be established for a candidate (unreadable/malformed/missing manifest, or a resolved install path that fails containment validation), the consumer MUST fail closed -- preserve the candidate rather than delete it -- and surface this to the user.

This should land as its own spec-editorial PR (with the matching `docs/public/specs/manifests/openapm-v0.1.requirements.yml` + Appendix C row and a `@pytest.mark.req("req-lk-0XX")` conformance test under `tests/spec_conformance/`), mirroring how `req-lk-020` itself was introduced as a defensive-clarification spec release (v0.1.13) rather than gating the original code fix. This mirrors `apm-spec-guardian`'s intended review path for spec changes.

## References

- PR: #2269
- Implementation: `src/apm_cli/deps/reachability.py`, `src/apm_cli/commands/uninstall/engine.py`
- Existing adjacent requirement: [req-lk-020](../blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/specs/openapm-v0.1.md#req-lk-020)
- Gate: `tests/spec_conformance/mode_b_detector.sh`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Mode B (silent extension)"

issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-07-18

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
1 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [B] Linear Scan Inside Loop -- src/apm_cli/commands/uninstall/engine.py:237-269

- Current: O(P x D) -- two separate linear scans over `lockfile.dependencies.values()` (size D) for every marketplace package in the uninstall list (size P). The outer loop at line 237 iterates `packages`; the first inner loop at line 248 scans all lockfile dependencies for an exact `(discovered_via, marketplace_plugin_name)` match; if that fails, a second inner loop at line 258 re-scans the same collection for a provenance-mismatch match.
- Proposed: O(P + D) -- pre-build two dicts once before the outer loop: `exact_index = {(dep.discovered_via, dep.marketplace_plugin_name): dep for dep in lockfile.dependencies.values()}` and `by_plugin = {dep.marketplace_plugin_name: dep for dep in lockfile.dependencies.values()}`. Each per-package lookup then becomes O(1).
- Fix: Build `exact_index` and `by_plugin` dicts from `lockfile.dependencies.values()` before the `for package in packages:` loop at line 237, and replace the two inner `for dep in lockfile.dependencies.values():` scans with dict lookups.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (418 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)
