#### `apm update` docs have an incomplete target list

- **Command**: `apm update`
- **Problem**: The `--target` option in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/update.md` lists only 8 valid target values, but the CLI accepts 20. The 12 omitted targets are valid inputs that will silently work but are not discoverable from the documentation.
- **Evidence**:

  Doc (`update.md`, options table):
  ```
  Accepts a single value (`claude`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `windsurf`, `kiro`, `codex`, `opencode`, `gemini`)
  ```

  Actual `apm update --help`:
  ```
  -t, --target TARGET  Agent target(s) to update for. Values: agent-
                       skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude,
                       codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork,
                       cursor, gemini, hermes, intellij, kiro,
                       openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf.
  ```

  Targets missing from the doc: `agent-skills`, `agents`, `agy`, `all`, `antigravity`, `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `hermes`, `intellij`, `openclaw`, `vscode`

- **Suggested Fix**: Replace the inline target list in `update.md` with the full set from the CLI, matching the format used in `install.md` (which already lists all values).

---

### Low Severity

#### Flag naming inconsistency: `--parallel-downloads` vs `--parallel-checks`

- **Commands**: `apm install`, `apm update`, `apm lock` vs `apm outdated`
- **Problem**: Three commands use `--parallel-downloads INTEGER` to limit concurrency; `apm outdated` uses `--parallel-checks INTEGER` with a unique `-j` short flag. While they control different underlying operations, users who expect a single consistent pattern across the CLI will find this surprising.
- **Evidence**:

  `apm install --help`: `--parallel-downloads INTEGER  Max concurrent package downloads (0 to disable parallelism)  [default: 4]`

  `apm outdated --help`: `-j, --parallel-checks INTEGER  Max concurrent remote checks (default: 4, 0 = sequential)`

- **Suggested Fix**: Either rename `--parallel-checks` to `--parallel-downloads` for consistency (with a deprecation alias), or add a note in the `apm outdated` reference doc explaining the naming difference. The `-j` short flag also has no analogue elsewhere in the CLI.

#### `apm deps update` has a stale target list (deprecated command)

- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: The deprecated `apm deps update` lists a narrower set of `--target` values than its replacement `apm update`. Users migrating to `apm update` may not realize additional targets are supported, and users still on the deprecated path cannot reach newer targets.
- **Evidence**:

  `apm deps update --help` target values:
  ```
  copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all

  copilot-cowork, cursor, gemini, hermes, intellij, kiro, openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf
  ```

  Missing from `apm deps update`: `agents`, `agy`, `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `hermes`, `intellij`, `openclaw`, `vscode`

- **Suggested Fix**: Since `apm deps update` is already deprecated, update its `--target` help text to reflect the current full target list so it matches `apm update`, or add a note that some targets require using `apm update` directly.

#### `apm config` description ends with a period; other command descriptions do not

- **Command**: `apm config`
- **Problem**: Minor punctuation inconsistency in help text style.
- **Evidence**:

  `apm config --help`: `Configure APM CLI.` (trailing period)

  All other top-level command descriptions (sampled): `Manage APM package dependencies`, `Initialize a new APM project`, `Install APM and MCP dependencies...`, `Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs` -- no trailing period.

- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the trailing period from the `apm config` description string to match the rest of the CLI.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks:

- **Error handling**: All tested commands (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with missing arg, `apm config set` with missing args, `apm mcp show` with missing arg) produce clean usage + error messages with no stack traces.
- **`--help` coverage**: Every command and subcommand responds correctly to `--help` / `-h`.

- **`apm mcp` subcommands**: `search`, `show`, `install`, `list` -- default values (list: 20, search: 10) match between CLI and docs.
- **`apm config` subcommands**: `get`, `set`, `list`, `unset` -- all present in CLI and documented accurately.
- **`apm runtime` subcommands**: `setup`, `list`, `status`, `remove` -- all present and consistent with `runtime.md`.
- **`apm lock export --format`**: README correctly states `apm lock export --format cyclonedx|spdx`; CLI confirms `-f, --format [cyclonedx|spdx]`.
- **Verbose flag**: `-v, --verbose` is consistently present and identically described on `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `run`, `deps update`, `mcp search`, `mcp show`, and `outdated`.
- **`--dry-run` flag**: Consistently named and described across `install`, `update`, `uninstall`, `compile`, `deps clean`.

issues.title: Fail closed when CLI is older than lockfile apm_version
issues.body:
## Problem

APM records the generating CLI in top-level `apm_version`, but current mutating commands validate `lockfile_version` without rejecting a running CLI older than that generator. A structurally compatible older CLI can therefore rewrite a newer-generated lockfile before the operator realizes that the tool itself is stale.

This was reproduced downstream with APM 0.24.0 against a lockfile generated by 0.25.0: the older CLI rewrote the newer lockfile. Refreshing dependencies or deleting caches cannot correct this because neither upgrades the running CLI.

Downstream evidence: https://gitlab.com/spiritt/tenants/spiritt/coding-agent-kit/-/issues/256

## Requested behavior

Before any command that may write `apm.lock.yaml`:

1. Read the single top-level `apm_version` when a lockfile exists.
2. Detect the running CLI version.
3. Fail before mutation when the CLI is older than the lockfile generator.
4. Name both versions and recommend `apm self-update` or a documented compatible installer.
5. Treat malformed or duplicate version metadata as unsafe rather than silently continuing.
6. Keep dependency/cache failures distinct from CLI compatibility failures.

The comparison needs to support APM's accepted prerelease forms (`aN`, `bN`, `rcN`) as well as stable releases. Build metadata should not affect precedence.

## Acceptance evidence

- A 0.24.0 CLI is rejected before writing a lockfile generated by 0.25.0.
- Equal and newer CLIs continue normally.
- Stable/prerelease ordering is covered.
- The rejected command leaves the lockfile byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The guard covers every mutating path, not only `install`.

## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-07-23
**APM Version**: 0.26.0 (64a7fb5)
**Commands Inspected**: 27 (top-level + all requested subcommands + runtime/mcp extras)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 0     |
| Medium   | 1     |
| Low      | 1     |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm deps update --target` help text lists stale/incomplete target values

- **Command**: `apm deps update --target`
- **Problem**: The help text for the deprecated `apm deps update` command lists only 10 target values: `copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills`. However, newer targets introduced in `apm update` and `apm install` -- specifically `agents`, `agy`, `copilot-app`, `hermes`, `intellij`, `openclaw`, `vscode` -- are NOT listed. Importantly, these unlisted targets ARE accepted at runtime (verified by running `apm deps update --target vscode`, which runs without a validation error). The help text therefore gives users a false picture of what is and is not valid.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps update --help
  ...
  -t, --target TARGET  Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                       copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex,
                       gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-
                       skills, all.
  ...
  $ apm update --help
  ...
  -t, --target TARGET  Agent target(s) to update for. Values: agent-
                       skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude,
                       codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork,
                       cursor, gemini, hermes, intellij, kiro,
                       openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf.
  ```
  `$ apm deps update --target vscode` runs without a target-validation error, confirming the value is accepted.
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--target` option help string in `apm deps update` to match the full canonical target list used by `apm update` / `apm install`, or delegate the help text to the same constant so it stays in sync automatically. Since the command is deprecated, a minimal fix is a one-line note: "Accepts the same target values as `apm update`; see `apm update --help` for the full list."

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm mcp install --help` forwarded flags not surfaced as formal CLI options

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: `apm mcp install` is a thin forwarder for `apm install --mcp`. The flags it forwards (`--transport`, `--url`, `--env`, `--header`, `--registry`, `--mcp-version`, `--dev`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--verbose`, `--no-policy`) are documented only in the description body of the help output, not as formal Click options. As a result, shell autocomplete tools and any help-parser that reads the `Options:` section will show only `--help`, making the command appear to accept no configuration.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp install --help
  Usage: apm mcp install [OPTIONS] NAME

    Add an MCP server to apm.yml. Alias for 'apm install --mcp'.
    ...
    Forwarded install options (see 'apm install --help' for the full list):
      --transport [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http]
      --url URL           Server URL for remote transports
      ...

  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.   <-- only formal option
  ```
  The flags ARE functional (`apm mcp install testname --transport http` runs without an unknown-option error), they are just invisible to autocomplete.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) declare the forwarded flags as explicit Click options in the `mcp install` command so they appear in `Options:` and tab-completion, or (b) add a `See also: apm install --help` note that is prominent enough for users who discover the command via `--help` or `help` in their shell.

---

### Clean Areas

All of the following passed inspection with no issues found:

- **`apm --help`**: Comprehensive command listing with consistent workflow examples. All listed commands exist.
- **`apm init --help`**: Clear, consistent flag descriptions.
- **`apm install --help`**: Extensive flag set; all options clearly documented with accurate defaults (`--parallel-downloads` default `4`; `--frozen` and `--update` mutually exclusive behavior correctly described).
- **`apm uninstall --help`**: Minimal, consistent; flags match docs.
- **`apm update --help`**: Full target list, accurate flag descriptions, `-y/--yes` and `--dry-run` present.
- **`apm compile --help`**: `--all` and `--target all` (deprecated) correctly documented; `--no-dedup` alias for `--no-force-instructions` confirmed functional.
- **`apm run --help`**: Correctly labeled "(experimental)".
- **`apm deps list/tree/info/clean --help`**: Consistent with docs.
- **`apm deps why --help`**: Present in both CLI and docs; `--json` and `--global` flags correct.
- **`apm mcp list/search/show --help`**: `--limit` defaults match docs (list: 20, search: 10).
- **`apm config get/set/list/unset --help`**: All four subcommands present; docs and CLI consistent. `config get` with no arg and `config list` produce the same output as documented.
- **`apm runtime setup/list/status/remove --help`**: All subcommands present; `-y/--yes` on `remove` confirmed; `{copilot|codex|gemini|llm}` enum correct.
- **Error handling**: `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (no arg), `apm config set` (no arg) all produce clean, actionable error messages with no stack traces.
- **`apm --help` vs docs directory**: Every command listed in the CLI top-level help has a corresponding page in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`. No orphaned doc pages found for commands that no longer exist.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-07-24
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-07-24
**APM Version**: 0.26.0 (64a7fb5)
**Commands Inspected**: 27

Commands covered: `apm`, `apm init`, `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm update`, `apm compile`, `apm run`, `apm deps`, `apm deps list`, `apm deps tree`, `apm deps info`, `apm deps clean`, `apm deps update`, `apm mcp`, `apm mcp list`, `apm mcp search`, `apm mcp show`, `apm mcp install`, `apm config`, `apm config set`, `apm config get`, `apm config list`, `apm runtime`, `apm runtime setup`, `apm runtime list`, `apm runtime status`, `apm runtime remove`

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 1     |
| Medium   | 2     |
| Low      | 2     |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm compile` docs: contradictory alias description for `--force-instructions` / `--no-dedup` within the same file

- **Command**: `apm compile`
- **Problem**: `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/compile.md` documents the `--force-instructions` / `--no-dedup` flag pair **twice**, and the two entries describe the alias relationship in **opposite directions**. The CLI help text is authoritative and matches only the second (Content section) entry; the first (Output control section) entry is wrong.
- **Evidence**:

  Line 92 (Output control table -- WRONG):
  ```
  | `--no-dedup` / `--no-force-instructions` | Keep the instructions section in the compiled output even when target-native rule files ... Hidden alias: `--force-instructions`. |
  ```

  Line 113 (Content table -- CORRECT):
  ```
  | `--force-instructions` / `--no-force-instructions` | Include the instructions section in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md ... `--no-dedup` is a hidden backward-compat alias for `--force-instructions`. |
  ```

  Actual CLI help (`apm compile --help`):
  ```
  --force-instructions / --no-force-instructions
      Include the instructions section in CLAUDE.md even when .claude/rules/ is
      already populated...Alias: --no-dedup.
  ```

- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the duplicate row from the "Output control" table (line 92). The "Content" table (line 113) is correct and should be the single authoritative entry. The primary flag pair is `--force-instructions / --no-force-instructions`; `--no-dedup` is the backward-compat alias -- not the reverse.

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm update` docs: `--target` flag lists only 8 valid values; CLI supports 20+

- **Command**: `apm update`
- **Problem**: The `apm update` reference doc (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/update.md`) lists only 8 target values in the `--target` flag description, while the actual CLI accepts over 20 values. The doc is significantly outdated.
- **Evidence**:

  Docs (`update.md` options table):
  ```
  Accepts a single value (claude, copilot, cursor, windsurf, kiro, codex, opencode, gemini) or comma-separated list
  ```

  Actual CLI (`apm update --help`):
  ```
  -t, --target TARGET  ... Values: agent-skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude,
                        codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork, cursor, gemini,
                        hermes, intellij, kiro, openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf.
  ```

- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--target` row in the `apm update` options table to include the full list of supported target values, matching the current CLI output. Consider linking to the targets reference page rather than duplicating the full list inline.

#### `apm compile` docs: duplicate flag documentation causes confusion even after fixing alias direction

- **Command**: `apm compile`
- **Problem**: Even setting aside the wrong alias direction in the "Output control" table entry (covered under High), having the same flag (`--force-instructions`) documented in two separate sections of the same page with different phrasings is confusing for readers. The "Output control" section entry uses `--no-dedup` as the primary name; the "Content" section entry uses `--force-instructions` as the primary name.
- **Evidence**:
  - Section "Output control": `| --no-dedup / --no-force-instructions | ...`
  - Section "Content": `| --force-instructions / --no-force-instructions | ...`
- **Suggested Fix**: Keep only the entry in the "Content" section. Optionally add a cross-reference note in the "Output control" section pointing to the Content section entry if the flag is conceptually relevant to output control.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm init` docs: `--target` valid values list omits newer targets

- **Command**: `apm init`

issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-07-29

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
1 finding identified.

### Findings

#### [C] Unconditional Expensive Operation -- Dual os.walk on same tree per compile run

**File:** `src/apm_cli/compilation/context_optimizer.py`
**Lines:** `_get_all_files` at 202-215, `_analyze_project_structure` at 452-500

- Current: 2 x O(n) `os.walk` passes over `self.base_dir` on every `apm compile`
  invocation. `_get_all_files()` walks to build `_file_list_cache`; then
  `_analyze_project_structure()` walks the same tree again to build
  `_directory_cache`. Both are triggered unconditionally inside
  `optimize_instruction_placement()` (lines 247 and 196 via `_cached_glob`).
- Proposed: 1 x O(n) walk that populates both caches in a single pass.
- Fix: Merge `_get_all_files` and `_analyze_project_structure` into a single
  `_build_caches()` method. In one `os.walk` loop, append each file to
  `_file_list_cache` and build each `DirectoryAnalysis` entry for
  `_directory_cache`. Guard both with the existing `_file_list_cache is None`
  sentinel so subsequent calls remain O(1).

**Frequency:** Once per `apm compile` run, but on large monorepos (thousands of
files) two full tree traversals are noticeably slower than one. The existing
`_cached_glob` / `_pattern_cache` guards eliminate subsequent walks, so the
merge is a one-time init cost reduction.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (418 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

### Notes

- Patterns A, B, D: No confirmed findings. The codebase consistently uses set
  objects for dedup / membership tests in loops (e.g. subsets.py, policy_checks.py).
  Config loads in script_runner.py are conditional re-fetches, not redundant ones.
- Pattern E: `from git.exc import GitCommandError` is imported at module level in
  `commands/update.py` (line 60), which is eagerly loaded by `cli.py` for every
  command. However, since `commands/update.py` also imports
  `deps.github_downloader` (which already pulls in GitPython), deferring
  `GitCommandError` alone would not meaningfully reduce startup cost. Low priority.
- Pattern F: subprocess calls in `cache/git_cache.py` and `deps/bare_cache.py` are
  per-package, but are already parallelized via `max_workers` parameters in the
  calling code (e.g. `resolve_revision_pin_updates`). No confirmed sequential I/O
  loop without existing concurrency guard.
- http_cache.py `_enforce_size_cap` already implements the tracked-size fast-path
  recommended by the pattern catalogue; no finding there.

issues.title: Extract shared retain/reindex predicate for git auth-config entries (follow-up to #2368)
issues.body:
## Description

PR #2382 (fixing #2368) added `set_authorization_header_git_env()` / `set_ado_bearer_git_env()` in `src/apm_cli/utils/github_host.py`. These rewrite the indexed `GIT_CONFIG_{COUNT,KEY_N,VALUE_N}` env-var set in place: existing auth-channel entries are stripped, everything else is preserved and re-indexed, and the new `Authorization` header is appended last.

That retain/reindex predicate intentionally mirrors the pre-existing `AuthResolver._clear_git_auth_env` in `src/apm_cli/core/auth.py` (same policy: an entry whose key contains `extraheader`, or whose value is an `Authorization:` header, is dropped; everything else is retained and re-indexed).

This is a genuine split authority per `.apm/instructions/architecture.instructions.md`: the SAME decision ("which `GIT_CONFIG_*` entries are auth-channel entries to strip") is now implemented in two places. If the predicate ever needs to change (e.g. a new auth-channel key pattern), only one site is likely to get patched, and the two will silently drift.

## Why this was not done in #2382

`_clear_git_auth_env` is a security-critical function that PR #2382 does not otherwise touch. The PR (and the apm-review-panel review, python-architect + auth-expert personas both flagged the same duplication independently) intentionally deferred this extraction to keep the original bug fix small, reviewable, and low-risk, rather than bundling a refactor of `_clear_git_auth_env` into a fix for a different, narrower defect.

## Proposed follow-up

Extract a single shared helper (suggested home: `src/apm_cli/utils/git_env.py`, a new module) that both `AuthResolver._clear_git_auth_env` (`src/apm_cli/core/auth.py`) and `set_authorization_header_git_env` (`src/apm_cli/utils/github_host.py`) delegate to for:
- parsing `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` (tolerating blank/invalid values),
- the auth-channel-entry predicate (`extraheader` in key, or value is an `Authorization:` header),
- retaining + re-indexing the non-auth-channel entries.

This PR should also update `.apm/instructions/architecture.instructions.md`'s canonical owner table to add a row for this newly-centralized decision (git auth-config retain/reindex), and add the dual guardrail required for a split-authority repair (behavioral regression test + a static boundary guard in `scripts/lint-architecture-boundaries.sh` + a matching `tests/integration/test_architecture_*.py` assertion + mutation-break evidence), since collapsing the two existing implementations into one is exactly the "split authority repair" case the architecture doc describes.

## Origin

Surfaced by the apm-review-panel (python-architect + auth-expert personas, independently converging) during shepherd-driver review of #2382. Cross-referenced via a `TODO` comment in `src/apm_cli/utils/github_host.py` next to `set_authorization_header_git_env`.

## Performance Scan - 2026-08-01

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
2 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [C] Unconditional directory re-read on every pattern cache miss -- src/apm_cli/compilation/context_optimizer.py:815-828

- Current: O(D) `iterdir()` syscalls per unique `apply_to` pattern not yet cached, where D is the number of project directories. For a project with P unique instruction patterns and D directories, this causes P*D filesystem reads during `apm compile`.
- Proposed: O(1) filesystem reads per cache miss by filtering the already-populated `_file_list_cache` (built by `_get_all_files()` via a single `os.walk`).
- Fix: In `_find_matching_directories`, replace `[f for f in directory.iterdir() ...]` with a pass over `self._get_all_files()` grouped by parent, so the existing `_file_list_cache` is reused instead of re-reading each directory from disk.

#### [C] Child-directory lookup via `iterdir()` instead of in-memory cache -- src/apm_cli/compilation/context_optimizer.py:850-855

- Current: `_calculate_inheritance_pollution` calls `directory.iterdir()` to find subdirectories that are in `_directory_cache`, paying an O(entries) filesystem read per call. This method is invoked per (directory, pattern) pair during placement optimization.
- Proposed: O(D) pre-built lookup of parent->children from `_directory_cache` keys, giving O(1) child enumeration per call with no additional syscalls.
- Fix: Build a `dict[Path, list[Path]]` children index from `_directory_cache.keys()` once in `_analyze_project_structure` (e.g., `{d: [c for c in _directory_cache if c.parent == d] for d in _directory_cache}`), then replace `directory.iterdir()` in `_calculate_inheritance_pollution` with a lookup into that index.

### Scan coverage

- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

issues.title: [BUG] apm pack does not produce bundle when dependencies: {}
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When `apm.yml` contains `dependencies: {}` (the key is present but the dict is empty), `apm pack --format plugin` does not create a bundle directory. Exit code is `0` and no error or warning is emitted — the pack silently produces no bundle output.

The root cause is in `src/apm_cli/core/build_orchestrator.py` inside `detect_outputs()`:

```python
if data and data.get("dependencies"):
    out.add(OutputKind.BUNDLE)
```

Python's truthiness treats an empty dict `{}` as falsy, so `OutputKind.BUNDLE` is never added to `outputs_needed` and `BundleProducer` is never called.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create an `apm.yml` with a `dependencies: {}` block and root-level `skills/`:

```yaml
name: my-plugin
version: 1.0.0
target: copilot

dependencies: {}
```

2. Add at least one skill file under `skills/my-skill/SKILL.md`.
3. Run `apm pack --format plugin --verbose`
4. Observe: no `build/` directory is created, exit code `0`, no error.

**Expected behavior**

The documentation states:

> `dependencies:` block present → a bundle

`dependencies: {}` has the block **present** — the key exists in the YAML. A bundle containing the package's own skills should be produced. The truthiness check should be replaced with an explicit `is not None` check:

```python
# Fix:
if data and data.get("dependencies") is not None:
    out.add(OutputKind.BUNDLE)
```

**Workaround**

Add any non-empty entry under `dependencies:` (e.g. a self-defined MCP server with `registry: false`). This makes the dict truthy and triggers `BundleProducer`.

**Environment**

- OS: Windows
- Python Version: n/a (using frozen binary)
- APM Version: 0.26.0
- VSCode Version: n/a

**Logs**

No error output — `apm pack` exits `0` silently when `dependencies: {}` is present. With `--verbose`, only the `PluginManifestProducer` output is shown (writing `.github/plugin/plugin.json` for `target: copilot`).

issues.title: [BUG] `--frozen` rejects repo-root claude_skill deps lacking apm.yml
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

Since v0.27.0, `apm install --frozen` fails with `--frozen: apm.lock.yaml is out of sync with apm.yml` for a **repo-root `claude_skill` dependency** — one whose repository root holds `SKILL.md` and no `apm.yml` (e.g. `makinux/adversarial-panel`) — whenever the project also carries MCP state. The reported reason is a missing `apm.yml` that such a package never has by design.

v0.27.0 extended `_enforce_frozen` to validate the MCP config view ([`install/service.py#L245-L270`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.27.0/src/apm_cli/install/service.py#L245-L270), added in #2390 / 47320354; v0.26.0's `_enforce_frozen` only ran `lockfile_satisfies_manifest`). That view walks the `apm.yml` of every locked dependency and records an absent one as a problem unless [`_allows_missing_manifest` — `integration/mcp_config_view.py#L209-L236`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.27.0/src/apm_cli/integration/mcp_config_view.py#L209-L236) permits it. That helper gates the `claude_skill` exemption behind `is_virtual_subdirectory()`:

```python
if dependency.package_type == PackageType.SKILL_BUNDLE.value:
    return True

dependency_ref = dependency.to_dependency_ref()
if not dependency_ref.is_virtual_subdirectory():
    return False
...
package_type, _ = detect_package_type(package_dir)
return (
    package_type is PackageType.CLAUDE_SKILL
    and dependency.package_type == PackageType.CLAUDE_SKILL.value
)
```

A repo-root skill is declared as a plain `owner/repo`, so its `virtual_type` is not `SUBDIRECTORY` ([`models/dependency/reference.py#L262-L275`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.27.0/src/apm_cli/models/dependency/reference.py#L262-L275)) and the function returns `False` before the on-disk shape is ever probed. A subdirectory skill such as `mattpocock/skills/skills/productivity/grilling` reaches the probe and passes, so only the repo-root shape is affected.

The gate is inconsistent with its own neighbours:

- The branch above it exempts `skill_bundle` unconditionally, without asking whether the reference is virtual.
- The probe below it already re-derives the type from disk, and `detect_package_type` classifies "root `SKILL.md`, no `apm.yml`" as `CLAUDE_SKILL` by documented cascade rule 3 ([`models/validation.py#L248-L279`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.27.0/src/apm_cli/models/validation.py#L248-L279)). The probe would accept this package if it were allowed to run.

The lockfile entry is not stale: a lockfile freshly generated by 0.27.0 records `package_type: claude_skill` for this dependency, and `apm audit` on the same tree reports `No drift detected` / `no issues found`. Only `--frozen` calls the state out of sync.

The check runs when `check_mcp` is true — `bool(root_mcp) or bool(lockfile.mcp_configs) or bool(lockfile.mcp_servers)` ([`install/service.py#L245-L247`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.27.0/src/apm_cli/install/service.py#L245-L247)) — so a project that declares no MCP server is unaffected. Combining a repo-root Claude skill with any MCP server makes `--frozen` permanently unusable: the advice `re-run 'apm install' to restore it` cannot succeed, because no `apm install` will ever produce an `apm.yml` for that package.

## To Reproduce

1. Create a project whose `apm.yml` declares a repo-root Claude skill and one MCP server.
   ```yaml
   name: frozen-repro
   version: 1.0.0
   description: Minimal reproduction for --frozen rejecting a repo-root Claude skill.

   targets:
     - claude

   dependencies:
     apm:
       - makinux/adversarial-panel
     mcp:
       - name: deepwiki
         registry: false
         transport: http
         url: https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp
   ```
2. Install normally to materialise `apm_modules/` and generate the lockfile.
   ```
   apm install
   ```
   → Succeeds. `apm_modules/makinux/adversarial-panel/` contains `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `assets/` and no `apm.yml`; the lockfile records `package_type: claude_skill`.
3. Re-run the same install with `--frozen`, changing nothing in between.
   ```
   apm install --frozen
   ```
   → Fails with `package manifest not found at .../apm_modules/makinux/adversarial-panel/apm.yml`.
4. Control: repeat steps 1–3 in a fresh directory with the `mcp:` block removed.
   → `apm install --frozen` succeeds and reports `No changes -- install state already up to date`.

## Expected behavior

- `--frozen` should not report an absent `apm.yml` as lockfile drift when the locked package is a `claude_skill` and the installed directory's shape is a valid Claude skill. Whether the dependency was declared as a repo root or as a subdirectory does not change the fact that the package ships no `apm.yml` by design.
- Concrete fix: in `_allows_missing_manifest` ([`integration/mcp_config_view.py#L217-L219`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/v0.27.0/src/apm_cli/integration/mcp_config_view.py#L217-L219)), drop the `is_virtual_subdirectory()` early return and let the two existing branches decide:
  - materialised `package_dir` → the strict shape probe already runs and still rejects a mislabeled or malformed package, so the guard it provides is not weakened;
  - absent `package_dir` (the cold-cache `apm audit --ci` case the comment describes) → the frozen lockfile classification `claude_skill` is already the documented fallback, and a repo-root skill fits it for the same reason a subdirectory one does.

  If the early return is to be kept, the minimal alternative is to extend the condition so a locked `claude_skill` also passes it, e.g. `if not (dependency_ref.is_virtual_subdirectory() or dependency.package_type == PackageType.CLAUDE_SKILL.value): return False`.

  This is the general rule #2207 already asked for — *"it should treat the lockfile package type / installed marker as the authority for whether an absent package manifest is expected rather than reporting every non-`skill_bundle` absence as corruption"*. The merged exemption instead keyed on virtuality, which is why the repo-root shape was left out.
- Independently of which fix is chosen: a problem that no user action can clear should not be reported with `re-run 'apm install' to restore it`.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 27.0 (build 26A5388g), arm64
- Python Version: Homebrew-distributed prebuilt binary (PyInstaller bundle; interpreter not visible to the user)
- APM Version: 0.27.0 (703dd9e)
- VSCode Version: N/A

## Logs

Step 3 — `apm install --frozen` on a tree that `apm install` has just produced:

```
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
[x] --frozen: apm.lock.yaml is out of sync with apm.yml.
  - makinux/adversarial-panel: package manifest not found at
/path/to/repro/apm_modules/makinux/adversarial-panel/apm.yml; re-run 'apm
install' to restore it
[i] Tip: run 'apm outdated' to see what changed, then 'apm update'.
[x] Install failed after 0.0s.
```

Step 4 — the same dependency at the same commit, with the `mcp:` block removed:

```
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
[i] Targets: claude  (source: apm.yml)
  [+] makinux/adversarial-panel @6b1061b5 (cached)
  |-- (files unchanged)
[i] No changes -- install state already up to date in 0.1s.
```

`apm audit` on the failing tree of step 3:

```
[>] Scanning installed packages and deployed files...
[>] Replaying install (cache-only)...
[+] Replayed 1 package(s)
[>] Diffing scratch vs working tree...
[+] No drift detected

[*] 12 file(s) scanned -- no issues found
```

Lockfile entry for the rejected dependency, as generated by 0.27.0 in step 2:

```yaml
- repo_url: makinux/adversarial-panel
  name: adversarial-panel
  host: github.com
  resolved_commit: 6b1061b50dbe27613f0e0b2b90882d297ed46a29
  version: unknown
  package_type: claude_skill
```

## Additional context

### Regression boundary

v0.26.0's `_enforce_frozen` ended at the manifest comparison and never consulted the MCP config view:

```python
satisfied, reasons = lockfile_satisfies_manifest(lockfile, manifest_deps)
if not satisfied:
    raise FrozenInstallError(
        "--frozen: apm.lock.yaml is out of sync with apm.yml.",
        reasons=reasons,
    )
```

`_allows_missing_manifest` carried the same `is_virtual_subdirectory()` gate in v0.26.0, but nothing on the `--frozen` path reached it, so the defect only became observable once #2390 wired the view into `_enforce_frozen`. `apm install --help` documents the new scope as *"including MCP config state"*.

### Impact

This blocks the CI-safe install path (`--frozen`) for any project that combines an MCP server with a repo-root Claude skill, with no in-project workaround short of dropping one of the two or abandoning `--frozen`. In my case it broke an unattended dotfiles bootstrap that runs `apm install --global --frozen`.

### Related — and why this is not a duplicate

`_allows_missing_manifest` has an existing lineage of manifest-less `claude_skill` reports. **Every one of them concerns a virtual subdirectory dependency**, which is precisely the shape the current exemption covers; none covers the repo-root shape, so this case has remained broken through all of them:

- #2213 — `config-consistency` requires `apm.yml` for `is_virtual` packages (0.25.0 regression). Fixed by #2214, which introduced the `is_virtual_subdirectory()` exemption that this report identifies as too narrow.
- #2207 — `audit config-consistency` rejects valid virtual `claude_skill` deps without `apm.yml`. Same virtual-subdirectory shape.
- #2328 — the virtual exemption denied in setup-only CI because the on-disk probe sees an unpopulated `apm_modules/`. Fixed by #2329, which added the cold-cache fallback (`if not package_dir.exists(): return dependency.package_type == PackageType.CLAUDE_SKILL.value`) — again reachable only after the virtuality gate.

Other context:

- #2390 — the PR that introduced the MCP config-view check into `_enforce_frozen`, which is what exposed the gate on the `--frozen` path.
- #2206 — a separate `claude_skill` defect on the `--frozen` path (lockfile churn from inconsistent `name`/`version`). Different cause; listed only because both concern how `--frozen` handles packages with no `apm.yml`.

I found no open issue, no open PR, and no discussion covering the repo-root `claude_skill` case.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-08-05
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-08-05
**APM Version**: 0.28.0 (dcbaf65)
**Commands Inspected**: 22 (top-level + all subcommands listed in task)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm deps update --target` lists a stale, incomplete set of targets
- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: The `--target` flag in `apm deps update` enumerates only 11 targets (`copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all`), missing at least 10 targets present in the canonical `apm update` and `apm install` flag help: `agents`, `agy`, `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `grok-build`, `grok-cloud`, `hermes`, `intellij`, `openclaw`, `vscode`. The `all` expansion description is also outdated (`all = copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+windsurf+kiro`) and omits newer targets. Even though `deps update` is deprecated, the stale target list can mislead users who are still using it during migration.
- **Evidence** (from `apm deps update --help`):
```
  -t, --target TARGET  Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                       copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex,
                       gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-
                       skills, all. 'all' = copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+windsurf+kiro
```
  Canonical list from `apm update --help`:
```
  -t, --target TARGET  Agent target(s) to update for. Values: agent-
                       skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude,
                       codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork,
                       cursor, gemini, grok-build, grok-cloud,
                       hermes, intellij, kiro, openclaw, opencode,
                       vscode, windsurf.
```
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--target` help string in the `deps update` command to reference the same shared target catalog used by `apm install` and `apm update`, or reference the canonical help text from those commands. Since `deps update` is deprecated, adding a note pointing users to `apm update --help` for the current target list would also be acceptable.

---

#### `compile` docs have two conflicting entries for the `--no-dedup`/`--force-instructions` flag
- **Command**: `apm compile`
- **Problem**: The `compile.md` reference page contains two separate table entries that describe the same underlying flag (`--force-instructions / --no-force-instructions`) with inconsistent naming and opposite descriptions. The first entry calls it `--no-dedup / --no-force-instructions` and describes it as "Keep the instructions section...", implying `--no-dedup` is the "enable" form. The CLI shows the true primary flag is `--force-instructions / --no-force-instructions` and `--no-dedup` is only a hidden backward-compat alias for `--force-instructions`. The first doc row reverses the expected naming convention.
- **Evidence**:
  - CLI help: `--force-instructions / --no-force-instructions ... Alias: --no-dedup.`
  - Doc row 1 (in "Modes" section): `` `--no-dedup` / `--no-force-instructions` | Keep the instructions section in the compiled output even when... ``
  - Doc row 2 (in "Content" section): `` `--force-instructions` / `--no-force-instructions` | Include the instructions section in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md even when... ``
  - These two entries contradict each other on which form is primary and on the described behavior.
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the `--no-dedup / --no-force-instructions` row. The canonical description belongs only under `--force-instructions / --no-force-instructions`; mention `--no-dedup` as a backward-compat alias within that single row.

---

#### `apm deps clean` is missing `-v, --verbose` flag
- **Command**: `apm deps clean`
- **Problem**: `apm deps clean` is a destructive write operation (removes all of `apm_modules/`) but exposes no verbose flag. Every other destructive write command (`install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `deps update`) supports `-v, --verbose`. Without it, users have no way to get detailed output during a clean operation.
- **Evidence** (from `apm deps clean --help`):
```
Options:
  --dry-run  Show what would be removed without removing
  -y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt
  --help     Show this message and exit.
```
  Compare with `apm uninstall --help`:
```
  -v, --verbose  Show detailed removal information
```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-v, --verbose` to `apm deps clean` with the description "Show detailed removal information" to match the pattern used by sibling commands.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm compile --legacy-skill-paths` help text implies it does something it does not
- **Command**: `apm compile`
- **Problem**: The `compile` CLI help text for `--legacy-skill-paths` reads "Deploy skill files to per-client paths... Compatibility flag for projects that need per-client skill layouts." This implies `apm compile` deploys skill files. The documentation explicitly states the flag is a no-op in `compile`: "Accepted for compatibility; skill deployment happens in `apm install` / `apm deps update`, not `apm compile`."
- **Evidence**:
  - CLI: `--legacy-skill-paths  Deploy skill files to per-client paths (e.g. .cursor/skills/)...`
  - Doc (`compile.md`): `| --legacy-skill-paths | Accepted for compatibility; skill deployment happens in apm install / apm deps update, not apm compile. |`
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--legacy-skill-paths` help string in `compile` to match the docs: "Accepted for compatibility; skill deployment happens in apm install / apm deps update, not apm compile."

---

#### Minor wording inconsistency in `--verbose` flag descriptions
- **Command**: Multiple
- **Problem**: The description of `-v, --verbose` varies across commands without a clear pattern. Examples: `init` says "Show detailed output", `install` says "Show detailed installation information", `uninstall` says "Show detailed removal information", `update` says "Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics". The first two are slightly different levels of specificity; no single standard phrasing is followed.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm init --help`: `-v, --verbose  Show detailed output`
  - `apm install --help`: `-v, --verbose  Show detailed installation information`
  - `apm update --help`: `-v, --verbose  Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics`
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize on `"Show detailed <verb> information"` where `<verb>` matches the command (e.g., `"Show detailed initialization information"` for `init`). Alternatively, adopt a single generic phrasing such as `"Enable verbose output"` across all commands.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks:

- `apm --help`: Top-level help is well-structured with clear workflows section.
- `apm install --help`: Comprehensive and consistent with `install.md` documentation.
- `apm uninstall --help`: Consistent with docs and CLI behavior.
- `apm update --help`: Target list, flags, and docs are in sync.
- `apm compile --help`: Core flags consistent with docs (excluding `--legacy-skill-paths` noted above).
- `apm run --help`: Correctly labeled experimental in both CLI and docs.
- `apm deps list/tree/info/why`: All flags match docs.
- `apm mcp list/search/show/install`: Flag defaults (`--limit 10/20`) match docs.
- `apm config set/get/list/unset`: All subcommands present and consistent with docs.
- `apm runtime setup/list/status/remove`: All subcommands present; experimental label in both CLI and docs.
- `apm init`: Deprecated `--plugin` and `--marketplace` flags correctly documented in both CLI help and docs.
- Error handling: All tested invalid-argument cases produce clean, helpful error messages (no tracebacks).

issues.title: [FEATURE] support "guidelines" files
issues.body: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** I do not use 'instructions' files because they are triggered by the coding agent and lead to instruction bloat. **Describe the solution you'd like** I would like to find a way to carry markdown files containing rules and instruction but are NOT `*.instructions.md`. I call them `guidelines` (`*.guidelines.md`) and they differ from instruction files and skill by 2 differents manerd: - unlike instruction files, it is not the coding agent that choose to load them, it is the LLM by progressive disclosure from AGENTS.md (or constitution.md) - unlike skill, the instructions to load these file it NOT in the very file frontmatter, because I want to reuse guidelines from project to project, and I found that you cannot write a generic load instruction in the frontmatter. It works amazingly fine when the load instruction is in the AGENTS.md The most easy example is "git-commit-guidelines". For a git commit, there is no file pattern to match, and we only need to load it when creating a git commit. Ok this might have been in a skill frontmatter, but imagine you have 3 or 4 different projects in your VS Code workspace with different git commit rules, which one needs to be loaded ? If these rules are clearly identified from the AGENTS.md, their is no problem since it is a path relative to this file. They are stored in `.github/guidelines/*.guidelines.md` and would be sync exactly the same than [instructions](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/producer/author-primitives/instructions-and-agents/). **Implementation idea** I would make this feature as generic as possible, allowing user to define what needs to be copied and where (perhaps per coding agent customization). Layout: ``` my-package/ apm.yml .apm/ markdown/ guidelines/ python-unit-test.guidelines.md git-commit.guidelines.md ``` when apm installs on a project configured for Github copilot, this will simply recopy to ``` ./ .github guidelines/ python-unit-test.guidelines.md git-commit.guidelines.md ``` **Describe alternatives you've considered** - instruction files => no, I do not want the agent to inject in the context using file patter - skills => no, if several projects are active, loading instruction in the frontmatter might conflict. **Additional context** Happy to discuss about this idea Real life example in my project copilot-session-usage: - [git-commit-message.guideline.md](https://github.com/gsemet/copilot-session-usage/blob/main/.github/guidelines/git-commit-message.guideline.md): they are very detailed, and the model loads them automatically immediately before generating a commit message, not always - the pointer to this file is in [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/gsemet/copilot-session-usage/blob/main/AGENTS.md) - another guidelines about how my [knowledge base works](https://github.com/gsemet/copilot-session-usage/blob/main/.github/guidelines/knowledge-base.guidelines.md), same, this is loaded only when the agent decides to, not when the coding agent forces to - Thread on X about this question... [Am I the only one NOT using instruction files?](https://x.com/gsemetfr/status/2085667067521323066) - Presentation of the (simple) structure of [the project harness I always use](https://x.com/gsemetfr/status/2077498943085117460).

issues.title: [BUG] Plugin root skills/ overrides the plugin.json declaration: undeclared skills deploy, declared ones drop
issues.body:
A plugin's raw root `skills/` directory overrides its resolved `plugin.json` declaration, so the set APM deploys can differ from the set the manifest declares — in both directions.

Found while working on #2530; it is a distinct defect and is deliberately not fixed in #2536.

## Behavior

`_map_plugin_artifacts` resolves the manifest into `.apm/skills/`, where a declared `skills` array replaces default discovery rather than adding to it. Deployment does not read that result: it prefers a root `skills/` bundle whenever one holds at least one skill.

Three plugins, all with `skills/{a,b}` at the root:

| `plugin.json` `skills` | resolved into `.apm/skills` | actually deployed / selectable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `["./skills/a"]` | `a` | `a`, `b` — undeclared `b` leaks in |
| `["./skills/", "./extra/solo"]` | `a`, `b`, `solo` | `a`, `b` — declared `solo` dropped |
| `["./skills/a", "./skills/b"]` | `a`, `b` | `a`, `b` — agrees |

The first row is the more likely one in practice: a plugin that ships several skills but declares only the ones it wants published still gets all of them deployed, with no diagnostic.

## Reproduction

```
mkdir -p plug/.claude-plugin plug/skills/a plug/skills/b
printf '# a\n' > plug/skills/a/SKILL.md
printf '# b\n' > plug/skills/b/SKILL.md
printf '{"name":"p","version":"1.0.0","skills":["./skills/a"]}' > plug/.claude-plugin/plugin.json

mkdir -p consumer/.claude
printf 'name: c\nversion: 1.0.0\ntargets: [claude]\ndependencies:\n  apm:\n    - path: ../plug\n' > consumer/apm.yml
cd consumer && apm install
ls .claude/skills          # a and b; only a was declared
```

`apm install --skill b` is likewise accepted, because `available_skill_names` enumerates the same raw directory.

## The open question

Does declaring `skills:` in `plugin.json` opt out of default `skills/` discovery?

Normalization already answers yes — `_resolve_sources` uses the manifest value *instead of* the default. Deployment answers no. That internal disagreement is the bug; which answer is correct is a product decision.

If "declared paths are requirements" (per the Plugin collection section of the package-types reference) means the declared set is exhaustive, the fix is to let the resolved `.apm/skills/` win for `MARKETPLACE_PLUGIN` in `SkillIntegrator.skill_source_dir`. That would also make `"skills": []` mean "no skills" as documented, and would fail closed when a declared path is rejected for escaping the plugin root.

It is worth noting this changes what existing consumers receive: any plugin declaring a partial list would start deploying fewer skills. That is why it is filed rather than bundled into #2536.

## Notes

- `#2536` makes enumeration and deployment agree with each other, so `--skill` no longer reports a set that differs from what deploys. It does not change which of the two sources wins.
- Neither `dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-advanced` (declares the whole container) nor `DuendeSoftware/duende-skills` (declares all 24 individually) triggers this.
- Environment: reproduced against `main` at 3aa036554 on Windows 11.

issues.title: [BUG] `apm install --dry-run` creates `~/.apm/apm.yml`, `config.json`, and `apm_modules/` while reporting "no changes made"
issues.body:
**Environment:** APM 0.28.0 (e041462), installed via the `microsoft/apm` Homebrew tap. macOS (darwin 25.5.0), arm64.

---


**Summary**

`--dry-run` is not read-only at user scope; it bootstraps the user-scope root before printing that nothing changed.

**Repro**

```bash
rm -rf /tmp/fakehome && mkdir -p /tmp/fakehome
HOME=/tmp/fakehome apm install microsoft/apm-sample-package#v1.0.0 -g --target claude --dry-run
find /tmp/fakehome -maxdepth 3
```

Output ends with:

```
[*] Dry run complete - no changes made
[i] Dry run completed: would install no changes in 0.3s.
```

Yet the filesystem now contains:

```
/tmp/fakehome/.apm/apm.yml
/tmp/fakehome/.apm/config.json
/tmp/fakehome/.apm/apm_modules
```

**Expected**

`--dry-run` should not write to disk, or should state which files it will create as part of the plan.

issues.title: [BUG] `apm uninstall -g` leaves Copilot hook files in `~/.copilot/hooks/`
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Uninstalling a user-scope package (`apm install -g` → `apm uninstall -g`) removes
every other primitive it deployed but leaves its Copilot hook files behind in
`~/.copilot/hooks/`. The orphaned file is live wiring: Copilot CLI keeps firing a
hook belonging to a package that is gone from `apm.yml`, `apm_modules/`, and the
lockfile. Reinstalling never clears it either — the path is simply never a
deletion candidate.

Copilot is the only harness affected, and only at user scope. Uninstall's
file-level removal routes each lockfile `deployed_files` path into a per-primitive
bucket via
[`BaseIntegrator.partition_managed_files`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/base_integrator.py),
which walks a segment trie built from every non-`skills`/`hooks` primitive prefix
and falls back to the `skills`/`hooks` prefix tuples only when the trie yields no
match:

```python
if last_bucket is not None:
    buckets[last_bucket].add(p)
    continue
# Fall back to cross-target buckets
if p.startswith(skill_tuple):
    buckets["skills"].add(p)
elif p.startswith(hook_tuple):
    buckets["hooks"].add(p)
```

At user scope the Copilot target's
[`user_primitive_overrides`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/targets.py)
maps instructions to `PrimitiveMapping("", ".md", "copilot_user_instructions")` —
an empty `subdir`, so its prefix is the bare target root `.copilot/`. That prefix
becomes a catch-all trie node: `.copilot/hooks/<pkg>-<hook>.json` matches at the
first segment, `last_bucket` is set to `instructions_copilot`, and the `continue`
skips the hook fallback. The hook path is handed to
[`InstructionIntegrator.sync_for_target`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/instruction_integrator.py),
whose `copilot_user_instructions` guard narrows the prefix to
`.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` and discards it. No integrator ever deletes the
file, and `HookIntegrator.sync_integration` never sees it in `managed_files`.

Nothing shadows `.copilot/prompts/` or `.copilot/agents/` — they own deeper trie
nodes and win by longest prefix. Hooks lose because they are routed by the
fallback tuples rather than by the trie. At project scope Copilot hooks land in
`.github/hooks/`, outside the `.copilot/` root, so the shadowing never applies and
removal works. The other harnesses escape for a different reason: their hooks are
merged into a shared config (`.claude/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, …) and
cleaned by `_apm_source` marker rather than by `managed_files`.

The symptom resembles #2245 / #2250, but those cover the merged-hook JSON path;
this is the per-file deployment path and a different root cause. Same target and
scope as #2232, also a different cause.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. `cd uninstall-copilot-user-hook-orphan`
2. `make user` — installs a package holding one hook and one prompt to user scope
   (`--target copilot`) under an isolated fake `$HOME`, then uninstalls it
3. See the prompt is removed and reported (`Cleaned up 1 integrated prompts`),
   while `.copilot/hooks/hookpkg-notify.json` survives and no hook cleanup is
   reported at all
4. `make matrix` — repeats install + uninstall at user scope for every hook-capable
   harness; only `copilot` reports an orphan
5. `make project` — installs the same package at project scope across all those
   harnesses; every hook is removed

**Expected behavior**

`apm uninstall -g` removes the hook files it deployed to `~/.copilot/hooks/`, the
same way it removes the package's prompts, and the same way project-scope
uninstall removes Copilot hooks from `.github/hooks/`. After uninstall no
harness still fires a hook from the removed package.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux (Arch Linux)
 - Python Version: 3.14.6
 - APM Version: 0.28.0 (e041462)

**Logs**

`make user` — prompt cleaned, hook orphaned:

```
  [+] ./hookpkg (local)
  |-- 1 prompts integrated -> .copilot/prompts/
  |-- 1 hook(s) integrated -> .copilot/hooks/
  |   postToolUse: runs echo hookpkg-ran (notify.json)

[*] Installed 1 APM dependency in 1.9s.
--- deployed under ~/.copilot/ ---
./.copilot/hooks/hookpkg-notify.json
./.copilot/prompts/greet.prompt.md

[i] Uninstalling from user scope (~/.apm/)
[>] Uninstalling 1 package(s)...
[+] _local/hookpkg - found in apm.yml
[i] Removed _local/hookpkg from dependencies.apm in apm.yml
[i] Removed _local/hookpkg from apm_modules/
[+] Cleaned up 1 integrated prompts
[*] Uninstall complete: Removed 1 package(s) from apm.yml, Removed 1 package(s) from apm_modules/
--- after uninstall (prompt gone, hook orphaned) ---
./.copilot/hooks/hookpkg-notify.json
```

`make matrix` — user scope, every hook-capable harness:

```
claude: clean
codex: clean
copilot: ORPHANED ./.copilot/hooks/hookpkg-notify.json
cursor: clean
gemini: clean
windsurf: clean
```

`make project` — same package, project scope, all six harnesses:

```
[+] Cleaned up 1 integrated prompts
[+] Cleaned up 4 integrated commands
[+] Cleaned up 6 integrated hooks
[*] Uninstall complete: Removed 1 package(s) from apm.yml, Removed 1 package(s) from apm_modules/
--- after uninstall (no file still carries the hook command) ---
```

**Additional context**

Minimal reproduction: https://github.com/sproott/apm-bugs
(`make user` / `make matrix` / `make project` in
`uninstall-copilot-user-hook-orphan/`).

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-08-13
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-08-13
**APM Version**: 0.28.0 (3aa0365)
**Commands Inspected**: 28 (top-level + all subcommands including undocumented ones discovered during audit)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 1 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm deps update --help` `--target` help text word-breaks inside words
- **Command**: `apm deps update --help`
- **Problem**: The `--target` description contains the compound string `'all' = copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+windsurf+kiro` with no spaces. Click's word-wrapping algorithm cannot find a natural break point and splits words mid-token at standard terminal widths (80 cols). The result is `co` / `pilot` on separate lines and `wind` / `surf` on separate lines, which is confusing and hard to read.
- **Evidence** (at COLUMNS=80):
  ```
  explicit-only -- not part of 'all'. 'all' = co
                                  pilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+wind
                                  surf+kiro (excludes agent-skills and
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Replace the compound token with a comma-separated or space-delimited format that Click can wrap naturally. For example:
  ```
  'all' includes: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, windsurf, kiro
  (excludes agent-skills and antigravity)
  ```
  Source: `src/apm_cli/commands/deps/cli.py`

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm deps update --help` target value list is outdated vs `apm update --help`
- **Command**: `apm deps update --help`
- **Problem**: `apm deps update` is deprecated, but its `--target` help text lists an outdated set of targets that is missing several targets present in the canonical `apm update --help`. Users migrating from `apm deps update` to `apm update` may be confused by the different target catalogs.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm deps update --help` target values: `copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all`
  - `apm update --help` target values: `agent-skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude, codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork, cursor, gemini, grok-build, grok-cloud, hermes, intellij, kiro, openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf`
  - Missing from `apm deps update`: `agents`, `agy`, `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `grok-build`, `grok-cloud`, `hermes`, `intellij`, `openclaw`, `vscode`
- **Suggested Fix**: Since `apm deps update` is deprecated, either update its target list to match `apm update`, or add a note in the target description pointing users to `apm update --help` for the current target catalog.

#### `apm mcp install --help` forwarded options only visible in description, not in `Options:` section
- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: All the forwarded options (`--transport`, `--url`, `--env`, `--header`, `--registry`, `--mcp-version`, `--dev`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--verbose`, `--no-policy`) are listed in the description text, but the formal `Options:` section only shows `--help`. Users who scan the `Options:` section (standard CLI discovery pattern) will not find any actionable flags and may not realize the command supports these options.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
  The forwarded options appear only in the body text under "Forwarded install options (see 'apm install --help' for the full list)".
- **Suggested Fix**: Either register the forwarded options as proper Click options with `is_eager=False` and forward them explicitly, or add a note in the description directing users to `apm install --help` more prominently (e.g. at the start of the description rather than after the usage examples).

---

### Clean Areas

- **All 28 help pages respond without errors**: Every `--help` invocation returned exit code 0 with structured output.
- **Error handling is clean**: `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (missing arg), and `apm config set` (missing args) all produce clean usage errors with no stack traces.
- **Top-level command list matches documentation**: All commands in `apm --help` have corresponding pages in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`.
- **No undocumented commands**: All CLI commands discovered (`approve`, `audit`, `cache`, `compile`, `config`, `deny`, `deps`, `doctor`, `experimental`, `find`, `init`, `install`, `lifecycle`, `list`, `lock`, `marketplace`, `mcp`, `outdated`, `pack`, `plugin`, `policy`, `preview`, `prune`, `publish`, `run`, `runtime`, `search`, `self-update`, `targets`, `uninstall`, `unpack`, `update`, `view`) have corresponding documentation pages.
- **`--help` / `-h` consistency**: All commands and subcommands support `--help`.
- **`--dry-run` naming**: Consistent `--dry-run` across all commands that support it (`install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `deps clean`, `deps update`).
- **`-y / --yes` naming**: Consistent across `update`, `deps clean`, `runtime remove`.
- **`-v / --verbose` short flag**: Consistent `-v` short form across all commands that expose verbose output.
- **`-g / --global` naming**: Consistent across `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `deps list`, `deps tree`, `deps update`, `runtime` subcommands.
- **`-t / --target` naming**: Consistent across `install`, `update`, `compile`, `deps update`.
- **`apm mcp` subcommands match docs**: `list`, `search`, `show`, `install` all present and consistent with `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/mcp.md`.
- **`apm runtime` subcommands match docs**: `setup`, `list`, `status`, `remove` all present and consistent with `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/runtime.md`.
- **`apm config` subcommands match docs**: `get`, `set`, `list`, `unset` all present and consistent with `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/config.md`.
- **README command references are valid**: Every `apm` command referenced in README.md (`install`, `compile`, `lock`, `outdated`, `update`, `audit`, `doctor`, `run`, `self-update`, `marketplace`) exists in the CLI.

issues.title: feat(mcp): per-dependency `targets` scoping for `dependencies.mcp` entries
issues.body:
## Problem

Global MCP installs have exactly one reconciliation domain: every `apm install -g --only mcp` reconciles the whole MCP surface across every target it has previously touched. `--target` is per-invocation only, so:

- Sequential per-target invocations delete each other's servers (pass 1 `--target claude` with server A, pass 2 `--target codex` with server B → A is removed as stale).
- Per-server-per-agent scoping is inexpressible at global scope. A fleet where server X should reach only Claude Code and server Y only Codex cannot be modeled — a union-target invocation deploys every server (including auth headers) to every target.

Verified on apm-cli 0.28.0.

## Current behavior

The documented per-dependency `targets` field works for package (`apm:`) dependencies, but on `dependencies.mcp` entries the key is not part of the model — it is swept into the harness-specific `extra` passthrough (with an unknown-key warning) and flattened verbatim into the deployed config (e.g. it appears as a bogus `targets` property inside the `~/.claude.json` server object), with no scoping effect.

## Request

Honor `targets:` on `dependencies.mcp` entries with the same semantics as package dependencies: effective reach = install targets ∩ per-dependency `targets`, omitted = all install targets, and reconciliation/stale-pruning computed per target from the intersection rather than the whole surface.

## Related

- #1761 (env-backed HTTP headers for Codex remotes) — same motivation: per-target differences in what should reach each harness.
- #2548 — the imperative `-g --mcp` path; the declarative manifest path this request builds on is the working one.

Context: building fleet tooling that generates `~/.apm/apm.yml` per host from a shared config; per-agent MCP scoping is currently the one thing forcing servers to stay outside APM.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-08-18
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-08-18
**APM Version**: `Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.28.0 (8993dcc)`
**Commands Inspected**: 26 (top-level + all required subcommands + additional: `mcp list`, `deps why`, `config unset`)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 0     |
| Medium   | 2     |
| Low      | 4     |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm compile` one-line description is inaccurate
- **Command**: `apm compile`
- **Problem**: The CLI description says "Compile APM context into distributed AGENTS.md files" but the command actually writes CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, copilot-instructions.md, and other per-harness files depending on the target. The description implies only AGENTS.md files are written, which is misleading to new users.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm --help` shows: `compile       Compile APM context into distributed AGENTS.md files`
  - `apm compile --help` shows the same one-liner, yet its own option descriptions reference CLAUDE.md: `Write AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md outputs under DIR instead of $PWD`
  - Docs (`compile.md`) correctly states: "Compile your instructions primitives into the AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md root context files"
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the CLI description string to: `Compile APM context into per-target deployment files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, etc.)`

---

#### `apm mcp install --help` lists forwarded options in description body instead of as structured Options
- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: The `--help` output shows forwarded options (`--transport`, `--url`, `--env`, `--header`, `-t/--target`, `--registry`, `--mcp-version`, `-g/--global`, `--trust-transitive-mcp`, `--dev / --dry-run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy`) only as inline text in the description body — not as structured `Options:` block entries. This is inconsistent with every other command in the CLI, makes the flags undiscoverable for tooling that parses `--help` output, and hides the `--dry-run` option which users expect to find in a standard options listing.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Usage: apm mcp install [OPTIONS] NAME

    Add an MCP server to apm.yml. Alias for 'apm install --mcp'.
    ...
    Forwarded install options (see 'apm install --help' for the full list):
      --transport [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http]
      --url URL              Server URL for remote transports
      ...
      --dev / --dry-run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy

  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
  Only `--help` appears in the structured `Options:` section.
- **Suggested Fix**: Declare the most common forwarded options (`--transport`, `--url`, `--env`, `--header`, `-t/--target`, `--dry-run`, `-v/--verbose`, `-g/--global`) as explicit Click parameters that pass through to `apm install --mcp`, so they appear in the structured options block. Less common flags can keep the "see `apm install --help`" note.

---

### Low Severity

#### Inconsistent `-v, --verbose` descriptions across commands
- **Commands**: `apm init`, `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm update`, `apm compile`, `apm run`, `apm mcp search`, `apm mcp show`, `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: The description for `--verbose` varies across every command with no consistent phrasing, making it harder to understand the flag at a glance.
- **Evidence**:
  - `init`, `run`: `Show detailed output`
  - `install`: `Show detailed installation information`
  - `uninstall`: `Show detailed removal information`
  - `update`: `Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics`
  - `compile`: `Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis`
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize to a consistent base phrase — e.g., `Enable verbose output` or `Show detailed output` — optionally appending a command-specific note where useful.

---

#### `apm deps tree` and `apm deps list` missing `-v, --verbose` flag present in sibling commands
- **Commands**: `apm deps tree`, `apm deps list`
- **Problem**: `apm deps update` supports `-v, --verbose`, but `apm deps tree` and `apm deps list` do not. Running `apm deps tree -v` produces an error. The absence is inconsistent within the `deps` command group.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps tree -v
  Error: No such option: -v
  ```
  `apm deps update --help` shows: `-v, --verbose  Show detailed update information`
  `apm deps list --help` and `apm deps tree --help` have no `-v` option.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-v, --verbose` to `apm deps list` and `apm deps tree` to show additional metadata (e.g., lock source URLs, commit SHAs, primitive file paths).

---

#### `apm deps update` docs table missing deprecation marker
- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: The `deps.md` reference docs table lists `update` without a deprecation notice, while the CLI itself clearly marks it as `DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead (strict superset)`. A user reading only the docs table would not know the subcommand is deprecated.
- **Evidence**:
  - Docs table (`deps.md`): `| update [PACKAGES...] | Re-resolve git refs and reinstall. |`
  - CLI (`apm deps --help`): `update  DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead (strict superset).`
  - (A `:::caution[Deprecated]` block does exist in the docs body, but not in the table.)
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the docs table row to: `| ~~update~~ [PACKAGES...] (deprecated) | Deprecated: use \`apm update\` instead. Re-resolve git refs and reinstall. |`

---

#### `apm deps clean` description wording mismatch between CLI and docs
- **Command**: `apm deps clean`
- **Problem**: The CLI help says "Remove all APM dependencies" while the docs say "Remove the entire `apm_modules/` directory." These are semantically equivalent but the CLI description is less precise — it doesn't clarify that this removes the `apm_modules/` directory, not the `apm.yml` declarations.
- **Evidence**:
  - CLI (`apm deps clean --help`): `Remove all APM dependencies`
  - Docs (`deps.md`): `| clean | Remove the entire \`apm_modules/\` directory. |`
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the CLI description to: `Remove the apm_modules/ directory (does not modify apm.yml)`

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks with no issues found:

- `apm init`, `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm update` — options complete, accurate, and consistent.
- `apm run` — experimental label present in both top-level and subcommand help.
- `apm deps list`, `apm deps tree`, `apm deps info`, `apm deps why` — descriptions and docs accurate.
- `apm mcp search`, `apm mcp show`, `apm mcp list` — consistent option blocks with `-v, --verbose` and `--limit`.
- `apm config`, `apm config set`, `apm config get`, `apm config list`, `apm config unset` — options and behavior match docs.
- `apm runtime`, `apm runtime setup` — labeled experimental consistently; options accurate.
- Error handling — all tested invalid inputs (`--nonexistent-flag`, missing required args) produce clean `Error:` messages with no stack traces.
- Flag consistency for `--dry-run` — present everywhere expected (install, update, uninstall, compile, deps clean).
- `--help` / `-h` — works on every tested command and subcommand.
- `--yes` / `-y` — consistent on interactive commands (update, deps clean).

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-08-19
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-08-19
**APM Version**: 0.28.0 (8993dcc)
**Commands Inspected**: 28 (including all required commands plus mcp list, deps why, config unset, lock, lock export)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 2 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### Inconsistent Trailing Periods in Top-Level Command Descriptions

- **Command**: `apm --help`
- **Problem**: Roughly half the commands in the top-level help listing end their one-line summary with a period; the other half do not. This creates visual noise and signals a lack of a style standard.
- **Evidence**:

  Commands **with** trailing period (17): `approve`, `audit`, `compile`, `config`, `deny`, `doctor`, `find`, `install`, `lifecycle`, `lock`, `pack`, `prune`, `publish`, `self-update`, `targets`, `uninstall`, `unpack`

  Commands **without** trailing period (16): `cache`, `deps`, `experimental`, `init`, `list`, `marketplace`, `mcp`, `outdated`, `plugin`, `policy`, `preview`, `run`, `runtime`, `search`, `update`, `view`

  Example contrast:
  ```
  config        Configure APM CLI.
  deps          Manage APM package dependencies
  ```

- **Suggested Fix**: Pick one convention and apply it uniformly. The idiomatic Click style omits trailing periods from short one-line descriptions. Remove the trailing period from the 17 commands that have one.

---

#### Inconsistent Wording for the `-y, --yes` Flag Across Commands

- **Command**: `apm update --help`, `apm deps clean --help`, `apm init --help`
- **Problem**: Three commands share a `-y, --yes` flag for skipping confirmations, but each describes it differently, making the CLI feel inconsistent.
- **Evidence**:

  ```
  apm update:     -y, --yes   Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)
  apm deps clean: -y, --yes   Skip confirmation prompt
  apm init:       -y, --yes   Skip interactive prompts and use auto-detected defaults
  ```

- **Suggested Fix**: Standardise to a single description. Recommended: `Skip confirmation prompts (non-interactive / CI mode)` -- short, consistent, and informative for all three use cases.

---

### Low Severity

#### Inconsistent Deprecation Notice Formatting

- **Command**: `apm deps update --help` vs `apm unpack --help`
- **Problem**: Two deprecated commands format their deprecation notice differently in the help summary line.
- **Evidence**:

  ```
  apm deps update: "DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead (strict superset). Update APM dependencies..."
  apm unpack:      "[Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle into the current project. Use 'apm install <bundle-path>' instead..."
  ```

  `deps update` uses `DEPRECATED:` (screaming-case prefix); `unpack` uses `[Deprecated]` (bracketed title-case).

- **Suggested Fix**: Pick one convention. `[Deprecated]` is softer and consistent with many CLIs -- apply it to both.

---

#### No Examples Section in Most Subcommand Help Texts

- **Command**: `apm init`, `apm compile`, `apm update`, `apm uninstall`, `apm config set/get/list`, `apm deps list/tree/info/clean`, `apm runtime setup`, and more
- **Problem**: Only `apm mcp install` and `apm view` (among the 28 commands inspected) include an inline `Examples:` block. Most commands have none, even for commands with non-obvious usage patterns (e.g. `apm deps why`, `apm config get`).
- **Evidence**: Running `apm init --help`, `apm config set --help`, `apm deps info --help`, etc. shows no examples section.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add 1-2 illustrative examples to each subcommand help text. The `apm mcp install` and `apm view` help texts are good models to follow.

---

### Clean Areas

The following areas passed all checks with no issues found:

- **Command/doc parity**: Every command in the CLI has a corresponding page in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`, and vice versa (34 commands, exact match).
- **Error handling**: `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (no args), and `apm config set` (no args) all return clean `Usage:` + `Error:` messages with no stack traces.
- **Technical accuracy**: All flag names, default values, and argument shapes in help text match the actual CLI behaviour verified through invocation.
- **`--dry-run` consistency**: Present on all write commands where expected (`install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `deps clean`, `prune`).

- **`deps why` subcommand**: Present in CLI, correctly documented, `--json` flag works as documented.

- **Deprecated command marking**: Both `apm deps update` and `apm unpack` are clearly identified as deprecated in their help text (formatting inconsistency noted above, but both are marked).
